RESEARCH TOWARD FEWER THAN 208 STATES
29 October 2026 — prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov

OUTCOME
No validated machine with 207 states or fewer was obtained. This archive is
an audited comparison and reproducible research contribution, not a new207
construction or a state-count lower bound. The retained208 machine is credited
to the incoming proposals, not presented as a new result.

The five submissions in the two user-specified commits contain nine literal
208-state tables but only TWO rooted transition-graph isomorphism classes.
All use the same conditional-history identification of the172/211 roles;
there is no independent deletion to stack across these submissions.

NEW RESEARCH
* Source-boundary projection supplies sound overapproximating seven-cell
  guards from complete arbitrary-natural symbolic primitive contracts,
  including compressed unary/list interiors and exact blank startup.
* A head-offset quotient lemma permits a different head position at merged
  control boundaries, including initialization by blank-tape translation.
* Whole closed-loop pruning preserves source control flow under checked zero
  guards, but fewer primitive occurrences worsen the existing shared-tree
  representation:3909->3904 leaves,197->200 distinct syntactic DAG nodes.
* Deeper-history, neutral-helper, offset, two-row, source-window and guarded
  layout searches are negative within their explicitly stated finite scopes.

REPLAY (Python3.10+, standard library)
From the extracted root:
    python3 -B reproduce.py --receipt /tmp/below-u208-replay.json
The default is FULL: both inherited208 graph classes are rederived through
all5,084 symbolic contracts; both new boundary projections are rebuilt; the
bounded selector/offset synthesis family is rerun; applicable independent
finite checks also run under Python-O. Four independent jobs may run in
parallel. Temporary files are outside the sealed package. Assertions must
remain enabled for symbolic induction. A finite search is not a kernel proof.

TRUST BOUNDARY
The Con(U)/Con(PA) calibration is inherited from the supplied construction
lineage. This work adds ordinary mathematical arguments and executable finite
or symbolic checks, not a new end-to-end Lean/Rocq/MM0 certificate or exported
PA derivation. No unconditional nonhalting, global minimality, historical
priority or semantic impossibility of rejected bounded templates is claimed.
No 207-state construction was obtained in this bounded lane.

Read PROJECTION.md for the proof scope. The new method derives finite local

A cutoff failure is not evidence of semantic inequivalence or state minimality.

not literally only the unary U instances. The supplied reports explicitly

# Local research toward fewer than 208 working states

No accepted 207-state machine is supplied here. This is a bounded research
record. Two input graphs are representatives from the incoming History U208
packet pinned by the enclosing report; their bytes and hashes are in inputs/.
The history and compatibility graphs are not isomorphic. Other incoming
presentations are renamings, not independent reductions to stack.

1. Backward finite-history aliases and shared-branch folds use up to 12 old
   transitions of guard information and positive simulation segments of at
   most 60 transitions. The two input classes each admit 148 eligible
   noninitial state pairs and 122,544 fold actions. No new fold survives.
   An earlier depth 8/40-step pass is retained for provenance.
2. Exhaustive single-row actions with a 40-step exact one-transition macro
   contract yield 351 neutral rewrites in the history class and 357 in the
   compatibility class. They are equivalences, not state reductions. Shared
   representatives cannot be obtained merely by intersecting both rows'
   nonrecursive neutral alternatives in the history class.
3. A neutral helper rewrite can be combined with a shared-branch fold action.
   Each failed concrete fold trace identifies possible modified helper rows;
   only rows on that trace can fix that failure. The search tries the recorded
   neutral alternatives at those rows, then requires an exact composite proof
   at both merged controls and the modified helper. There are 3,138,357 and
   3,159,139 repair attempts respectively, with no accepted result. A helper
   that is not neutral on its own is outside this family.
4. Both rows of any merged noninitial pair may change, with no requirement of
   a shared literal row. Each class has 21,321 pairs. The guards intersect a
   nine-cell blank-run fixed point with depth 12 history information. Positive
   old and new blocks must join within 32 steps with identical head, control,
   and entire known window, without reading opaque exterior or reentering a
   merged control. Respectively 19,100,685 and 19,111,897 candidate actions were
   tested, with no accepted result. These sufficient templates are not a
   state lower bound.

The initial-control-inclusive variant also completed 207 pairs and 192,663
action trials in each class, with no result. The source-window-intersection
lane is bound only to the Entry primary class A table; it does not transfer
those guards to the nonisomorphic compatibility class. It completed 17,493 affected pairs (3,828 unchanged pairs covered by the
prior class A search were skipped), 15,388,630 action trials, with no survivor.
The raw receipt's `pairs=21321` is the final combination index, not the
number of affected pairs tested; `source_guard_stats.json` makes this
distinction explicit. Guard windows shrink from 26,731 to 20,547 across 119
states. The table and projection SHA-256 hashes are bound separately.

`python3 -B verify_neutral.py` and `python3 -O -B verify_neutral.py` freshly
re-establish all 708 recorded neutral identities against the literal input
bytes. This uses the inherited finite-history and branching macro engine,
not an independent proof assistant. It recomputes 42,240 history-context
checks and 24,987 consistent symbolic branch obligations. Inconsistent
read/guard combinations are vacuous.

The backward-history guards hold on every run from state 0 with any initial
tape. The forward local-window fixed point is weaker in scope: it begins
with a blank initial window and overapproximates new exterior bits. Their
intersection therefore holds for every blank execution. A successful
candidate would still require all construction-specific proof obligations;
no negative search receipt asserts that all smaller machines are impossible.

RESULT
======
machine/u208.tm is an explicit deterministic binary single-tape machine
with 208 working states, labels 0 through 207, and separate halt label 208.
Start state 0, head 0, blank tape; the initializer is included. All 416 rows
move L or R. Native labels are only names: native 211 is working, native 254
is halt. machine/state_map.json gives the exact native-to-dense bijection.

Dense SHA-256:
a2fee9e41311c0d43aaac871ea411be24eada17e6b3633c55f40b437101144e1
Native SHA-256:
b348a466a2c316511e0037ea3824de29d4c6ad37338404fbc98a3968fdb25135

Relative to the Joint U209 parent, the entire change is:
  delete state 172 (both rows)
  change 116/0 from 0 R 172 to 0 R 211
  change 211/0 from 0 R 157 to 0 L 217
Every other retained row and the complete source program remain unchanged.

The parent has two different reachable contexts: state 172 has preceding
bits 10, and state 211 reading 0 has preceding bit 1. A five-state inductive
invariant proves these facts on every initial tape from state 0. Four exact
local blocks of lengths 7, 1, 3, 1 and 414 ordinary row identities prove the
all-tape halting equivalence. The old/new first-halting clocks obey
  T208 = T209 + 6*N209(172,0) + 2*N209(211,0),
so T209 <= T208 <= 7*T209.

COMPARISON
==========
Six supplied U209 submissions give only TWO rooted labeled graph classes.
Plain, Compatible Folds, Composed, full Joint, and PDF-only Joint are class A.
Compatibility is class B. Compatible Folds and full Joint are byte-identical.
The PDF-only Joint table equals Plain, not full Joint byte-for-byte.
Both classes admit the new reduction. alternative/ contains the second,
nonisomorphic 208-state variant, using helper 214 instead of 217.

PROOF STATUS
============
The new local reduction has a complete ordinary mathematical proof and
small independent executable certificates. It is formalizable in PA.
Composing it with the retained source, numerical-calculus, startup, and
unary-theory arguments gives the PA-provable consistency equivalence:
  PA |- not Halt(U208,blank) <-> Con(U) <-> Con(PA).
There is no consistency assumption in this biconditional. Actual
nonhalting requires Con(PA). This release supplies no newly exported
end-to-end Lean, Rocq, or MM0 certificate for that endpoint and makes no
global minimality or independently ratified priority claim.

FRESH VERIFICATION
==================

* Independent comparison verifies all six tables and the same 3,909 primitives
  and 5,083 ordinal source control edges.

* Exact 208-state/416-row table and dense relabeling; 12 damaged controls

* Full fresh PRIMARY U208 symbolic replay: 5,084 arbitrary-natural primitive

* Exact 48,140-step blank startup, full trace and complete tape unchanged.
* Independent C++ finite regression: 15,252 cases, 6,778,830 literal primitive steps.
  The finite cases and 2,000,000-step blank prefix are NOT proofs of nonhalting.
* Alternative 208 has exact local/history construction checks. A separate
  universal runtime replay for the alternative is not claimed.

**There are only two machines up to rooted labeled transition-graph
isomorphism, not five or six independently different 209-state machines.**
The Plain, Compatible Folds, Composed, Joint, and PDF-only Joint tables form
one class. Compatibility forms the second class. Compatible Folds and the
full Joint ZIP contain byte-identical native and dense tables. Plain and
Composed differ only by permutations of a few internal decoder labels.

This statement was checked independently of every supplied checker, using
`inspect_tables.py`. The checker parses all literal rows, verifies totality,
the binary alphabet, directions, start and halt labels, and graph
reachability. It propagates the uniquely forced rooted map along read-zero
and read-one edges, preserving writes and directions. All 209 working
states and halt are graph-reachable in each table, so a consistent completed
map is a full isomorphism; a conflicting forced assignment disproves one.
This is graph reachability, not a claim that the blank run visits every state.

The PDF-only Joint is an especially important naming trap. Its Appendix B
was independently extracted to 418 rows, all of which match **Plain**
exactly. It does not identify the table in the full Joint ZIP byte-for-byte,
although that table is isomorphic. The PDF-only report describes a
30-rotation construction via Contextual U211, whereas the full Joint package
uses an explicit common source association. Its stated hash is accurate for
the machine actually printed in its appendix.

These two short permutations explain why distinct file hashes and different
construction recipes should not be counted as independent state-count

The common U212 ancestor has three deletions previously realized separately
by Contextual, Research, and Rotated U211. The U209 proposals arrange a
common source layout in which all three deletions coexist. They remove
native labels 180, 181, and 218. In class A the replacements are 163, 220,
and 157; in Compatibility the last stage replaces 180 by 216 instead of
163. These are contextual folds, not ordinary identical-row merges.

The common principle is that a state entered by a right-moving transition
which writes a fixed bit has a known predecessor cell. Two decoder modes
can therefore share one physical state when an existing helper recovers
the mode from that bit. The hard part is arranging source addresses so that
all incoming transitions have the required tags while preserving helper
entries from other parts of the interpreter.

Every construction retains the arithmetic-entry repair at native 171/read0,
changing its backward entry from state 7 to 205. The source decoder at 7
is shared with arithmetic execution; a source reassociation that forgets
this repair is invalid. The finite checkers explicitly test this case.

All proposals preserve the complete blank initializer. Their exact startup
check runs 48,140 transitions and verifies the complete canonical endpoint,
including 120 one-cells and both zero exteriors. The endpoint has native
state 84, head -2, source ordinal 136, header distance 56, registers
`[1,0,13,0,0,1,0,0,1]`, and 43 spare registers initially equal to one.
Preservation of this prefix is useful evidence about initialization, not a
proof of nonhalting.

The Plain package offers the most explicit rotation ledger: 30 closed
reassociations from U212, then the entry repair and simultaneous folds.
Its local quotient proof separates 414 ordinary rows from ten exceptional
two-cell cases. It audits all final internal-prefix bindings against the
simultaneous quotient and includes thirteen damaged controls. It clearly
distinguishes intermediate source identities from valid interpreters:
seventeen intermediate layouts have a seven-zero source run, and only the
final six-zero layout is used for the runtime theorem.

It also contains the strongest separate logical research result among the
packets: a proof that deleting the native dominated propositional axiom
destroys the desired PA calibration. The proposed Boolean matrix interprets
implication by Boolean equivalence, membership as false, equality as true,
and quantification as identity. It validates the other rows and U covering
bundles but makes target 1 false. PA can formalize induction on reduced
derivations, proving the reduced calculus's target underivability. Thus,
assuming PA is consistent, the reduced system cannot still have a
PA-provable equivalence with Con(PA). The word “dominated” in this lineage
describes a bound on a numerical parameter, not logical redundancy.

Its README accurately distinguishes freshly replayed original finite

checks. Its final table is identical to full Joint. The presentation

This supplies 30 rotations and a five-state label permutation, with an

The package recovers and includes the U222 calibration archive directly,
repairing a documentation omission in the compact inherited ancestry.
This improves provenance accessibility; it does not give a different
209-state machine up to isomorphism. Its reproduction command rewrites
generated machine/evidence files, so our replay used a separate copy.

Its additional searches record no direct state alias within 15 local
steps and no one-row opposite-tag fold within 17 local steps among the
tested family. The searches are explicitly incomplete. They do not
establish a 209-state lower bound or exclude source reassociation,
multi-row rewrites, longer macros, or invariants using more than one cell.

The full Joint package is a convenient evidence base for another class-A
reduction; Compatibility remains the distinct alternate source layout.

\subsection{Independent isomorphism and source checks}
A rooted read-labeled graph map is forced by following zero and one
edges from state~0. An independent breadth-first procedure propagates
that map, checking writes, directions, injectivity, and the distinguished
halt label. Every working state is graph-reachable in every table, so
a consistent map covers the whole machine. This is syntactic graph
reachability; it does not assert that the actual blank computation
visits every state.

In native labels, the nontrivial permutations are particularly small:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{Plain to Joint or Compatible Folds:}&
 (217\ 129\ 214)(215\ 204\ 216),\\
\text{Plain to Composed:}&(215\ 129\ 204\ 214\ 216).
\end{array}
\]
All other labels are fixed, including initial state~0 and halt~254.
The checker verifies the conjugacy of every row. For Plain versus
Compatibility, the forced map has an explicit conflicting assignment;
the witness is retained in \path{comparison/independent_comparison.json}.
Its edge words are paths in a labeled graph, not claimed tape histories.

The two source layouts differ in exactly 720 addresses. An independent
interval-based resolver verifies the same ordered 3,909 opcode/operand
pairs and all 5,083 guarded ordinal control edges. Both have maximum
consecutive-zero run six and 197 distinct source subtrees. Compatibility
reduces maximum address depth from 42 to 41. A shallower source tree alone
does not establish a better asymptotic runtime for the complete proof search.

\subsection{What is shared, and what each package contributes}
The U209 machines descend from one common U212 construction. Their
joint layouts allow deletion of native states 180, 181, and 218, which
had previously been removed separately in three U211 proposals.
Class A uses representatives 163, 220, and 157. Compatibility instead
uses 216 for state 180, with 220 and 157 serving the other two folds.
All packages retain the arithmetic-entry repair at native row $171/0$,
redirecting the backward entry from 7 to 205. That repair is necessary
because a source decoder also serves an arithmetic role.

The common reduction method exploits bits written immediately before
a decoder entry. Opposite predecessor bits allow two control roles to
share a state when an existing helper recovers the role from the tape.
The source reassociations ensure that the required tags coexist without
breaking the primitive control-flow graph or other interpreter entries.
Different deleted labels therefore do not automatically give additive
savings: the helper and address requirements can conflict.

\paragraph{Plain.}
This package gives a detailed ledger of 30 closed source rotations from
U212, explicit local quotient cases, and careful treatment of the
arithmetic entry. It distinguishes algebraic intermediate layouts from
valid final interpreters: some intermediate addresses have seven-zero
runs, while the final runtime proof uses the restored six-zero bound.
It also supplies a useful obstruction: simply deleting the apparently
dominated propositional row destroys the intended PA calibration.
A Boolean interpretation using equivalence as implication validates
the remaining calculus while keeping its target false. That is a
reason to retain the row, not an unexplored one-state saving.

\paragraph{Compatible Folds.}
Its staged 212-to-211-to-210-to-209 construction makes the coexistence
of the old three folds explicit. It is a useful presentation of the
same literal machine later delivered in the full Joint package.
The extra exposition is valuable even though it is not an additional
transition-graph class.

\paragraph{Joint, full package.}
This is the selected baseline for the new construction. Its direct
18-selector layout, compact complete ancestry, independent source-prefix
auditor, and finite C++ executor make it convenient to extend and review.
The selection is about its evidence organization, not a smaller state count
than the other class-A presentations.

\paragraph{Joint, PDF-only package.}
The report is readable and its printed table is complete, but it does
not add an executable verification package. Its table agrees with
Plain, not byte-for-byte with full Joint. This distinction matters when
binding a mathematical argument to a literal transition file.

The inherited runtime engines are essentially the same implementation
under label and import changes. Multiple passing receipts should not be
presented as independent logical foundations. The unary-theory
interpretation, native numerical calculus, strong compiler, and protected
startup argument are also shared. The new reduction preserves these
components and has a short separate local proof.

\subsection{Why the new fold was outside the old local search}
The retained Joint search tested direct aliases through 15 steps and
one-row folds using opposite unconditional predecessor tags through
17 steps. No result was found in those scopes. Native state 211 is
entered from both directions and does not possess a uniform predecessor
tag. Its useful property is conditional on reading zero; state 172
needs two predecessor cells. Extending the search to finite-history
contexts exposes this interface. The successful proof needs only the
five-state invariant and the four finite identities below, and does
not depend on search bounds or random screening.

RESULT
======
machine/u209.tm is a complete deterministic two-symbol, one-tape candidate
with 209 working states (0 through 208), separate halt label 209, initial
state 0, head coordinate 0, and an all-zero two-way infinite tape. Every one
of its 418 transitions moves L or R. Blank initialization is included.

\begin{proposition}[Uniform consistency reductions]\label{prop:theories}
There are PA-verifiable transformations of finite refutations yielding
\[
 \PA\vdash\Con(\ThU)\leftrightarrow\Con(\PA)
                 \leftrightarrow\Con(\ThW+\IR).
\]
The upper interpretation remains valid when ordinary equality and matrices
containing equality are permitted in the machine-facing presentation.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The first equivalence is the interpretation theorem proved in the supplied
report \cite{unary}, included in full under \texttt{references/theory\_U}.
Its relevant uniformity is summarized below. Since $\ThW$ includes every
$\ThU$ instance, a $\ThU$-refutation is immediately a
$\ThW+\IR$-refutation.

For the upper interpretation, interpret $E(x,a)$ as ``bit $x$ of the
binary expansion of $a$ is~1,'' and equality as arithmetic equality. PA
proves $E(x,a)\to x<a$ and hence irreflexivity. It also proves
$\Sub(x,a)\to x\le a$. For each fixed translated matrix
$\theta(x,a,\bar p)$, full PA induction constructs a number $b$ whose
1-bits are precisely the integers $x\le a$ satisfying
$\Sub(x,a)\land\theta(x,a,\bar p)$. Thus $b$ satisfies both weak-cover
clauses. This bounded finite selection uses the induction instance for the
particular formula $\theta$; it does not assume a uniform arithmetic truth
predicate. Arithmetic coding of exponentiation and finite bit sequences is
available in PA by its usual primitive-recursive definitional extensions.

Replacing each axiom in a $\ThW+\IR$ refutation by this finite arithmetic
derivation produces a PA-refutation. The $\PA$-to-$\ThU$ interpretation
then produces a $\ThU$-refutation. The translations are recursive on
formulas and finite proof lists, and PA verifies their correctness by
induction. The same upper argument handles equality-containing matrices.
\end{proof}
\subsection{The lower interpretation used from the supplied report}

For clarity about this dependency, the lower interpretation is much stronger
than an observed resemblance to finite sets. It uses coextensionality
$u\Eq v$ defined by
$\forall z(E(z,u)\leftrightarrow E(z,v))$, and numerical representatives
that are saturated, transitive, and linearly ordered by membership modulo
$\Eq$. Its endpoint condition requires each nonempty intersection of an
existing object's member profile with a numerical initial segment to have
least and greatest member classes. No external finiteness or well-foundedness
is assumed.

The dependency order is essential. Empty objects and local predecessor
facts are derived first. A unary filter of failures gives induction on
numerical representatives before total successor existence is known.
Parameters in an induction formula are internalized by a universally
quantified implication whose antecedent states that the corresponding base
and step premises hold. Induction then yields comparison and least failed
numerical tuples. Such least tuples permit bounded numerical comprehension
using genuinely unary matrices. For example, the matrix says that $z$
belongs to the definable profile associated with some least failing tuple;
the tuple is bound inside the matrix rather than used as an illicit free
parameter.

All the auxiliary definitions are fixed finite formulas. Once the
interpretation is fixed, its proof translation requires only structural
formula translation, fresh-name choices, finite proof concatenation, and
insertion into the induction template. The supplied paper explicitly gives
this PA-verifiable uniformity. We reviewed that mathematical argument and
replayed its delivered diagnostics, but have not produced a new kernel
formalization of it. Finite diagnostic success alone is not the reason for
Proposition~\ref{prop:theories}.

There are two standard equivalent ways to handle falsity. Decode $F$ as
$E(v_0,v_0)$ and normalize it under $\IR$, or decode an implication with
consequent~1 as ordinary negation. In either presentation, inside
$\ThW+\IR$ one has uniform proof transformations for
\[
 D(I(f,g))\leftrightarrow(D(f)\to D(g)),\qquad
 D(Q(i,f))\leftrightarrow\forall v_iD(f).
\]
The zero collapse is harmless because both $\top$ and $\top\to\top$ are
theorems. Treating code~1 as false without justifying irreflexivity would
be a genuine soundness error.

\paragraph{A second pitfall avoided.}
Using arbitrary source and tested labels $b,a$ would require a check
$a\ne b$: when $a=b$, the subset guard is tautological and the schema
becomes unrestricted comprehension. But applying that extra check to the
whole bundle would also suppress diagonal membership vacuity. Fixing the
power-cover roles to distinct labels~0 and~1 avoids both problems and
preserves the old logical interface.

One must not infer arbitrary primitive-equality vacuity from this alone.
The inherited proof instead interprets equality by two-sided membership
indiscernibility,
\[
 \operatorname{Eind}(x,y):=
 [\forall r(E(r,x)\leftrightarrow E(r,y))]\land
 [\forall r(E(x,r)\leftrightarrow E(y,r))],
\]
with fresh bound names. The \texttt{L224E}/\texttt{Interp222}
templates establish first-order completeness through that interpretation.
Their premises are exactly the retained logical rows and membership
vacuity just recovered. They do not use the Theory~K schema. Equality-free
formulas, including the $\ThU$ and $\ThW$ schemas, are unchanged by this
interpretation. All templates are finite syntactic proof transformations.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}

\subsection{Why proof-theoretic strength does not order state counts}

A consistency-search program's size depends on its axiom generator,
syntax, proof engine, and compiler. Proof-theoretic strength places no
monotone lower bound on those sizes: a stronger theory can have a shorter
presentation. Here the arithmetic interpretation appears only in the
correctness proof. The machine emits a short covering schema. Its state
cost is determined by using formula codes as fresh variable labels,
fixing source and test roles, retaining the membership-vacuity interface,
and sharing physical states.

\section{A smaller equivalent axiom-emitter source}\label{sec:source}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform equivalence in the common logical core]\label{lem:core}
For every natural \(a,b,c\), the retained numerical logical core proves
both \(I(B(a,b,c),B'(a,b,c))\) and its converse, by proof templates
primitive recursive in \(a,b,c\).
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The inherited dominated \(\rho_8\) derivations supply the ordinary
implicational \(K\) and \(S\) principles and antecedent exchange
\[
 A\to(B\to C)\ \longleftrightarrow\ B\to(A\to C).
\]
They use the retained logical basis and not the nonlogical covering axiom.
The unchanged generalization rule and \(\rho_2\) quantifier-distribution
row lift any proved implication \(A\to D\) to
\(\forall i A\to\forall i D\): generalize the implication at \(i\)
and apply the distribution row by modus ponens.

Apply exchange to \(G_c\to(c\to e_c)\), then lift it under the
quantifier at 1, obtaining \(L_c\leftrightarrow L'_c\). Implicational
congruence and another exchange give
\[
 L_c\to(U_c\to F)\ \longleftrightarrow\
 U_c\to(L'_c\to F).
\]
Lift this equivalence under the quantifier at \(c\) to obtain
\(H_c\leftrightarrow H'_c\). Finally use implicational congruence,
including contravariance of the antecedent, for the two outer implications
defining \(B\) and \(B'\).

Let \(\mathcal C\) and \(\mathcal C'\) be the old and new numerical
calculi. The same gate selects corresponding bundle families. Replacing
an old bundle-axiom leaf by its new counterpart and the reverse implication
from Lemma~\ref{lem:core}, followed by modus ponens, translates proofs
from \(\mathcal C\) to \(\mathcal C'\). The forward implication supplies
the reverse translation. Every other proof leaf and rule is unchanged.
PA verifies the translations by induction on finite proofs, yielding
\[
 \PA\vdash
  (\exists p\,\operatorname{Prf}_{\mathcal C}(p,1))
  \ \longleftrightarrow\
  (\exists p\,\operatorname{Prf}_{\mathcal C'}(p,1)).
\]
The detailed numerical derivations and the inherited theorem names are
included in the source-transport proof artifact. This argument avoids a
possible completeness circle: the new bundle's full first-order
interpretation is not needed to prove equivalence of the axiom families.

\[
 \forall s\;\exists C\;\forall x\,
 \bigl[(x\in C\to\phi(x,s,\bar p))\land

displayed formula is universally closed over \(\bar p\). Dependence on
the source \(s\) is permitted but not required. The accompanying \(\IR\) is

this presentation's consistency with unary theory \(\ThU\) and PA.

\section{Rejected leads and practical limits}

Shortening the zero-run detector by one state was rejected. Its blank
initialization reached a calibrated frame, but source site 26 had an
incorrect primitive successor on a concrete admissible register frame.
The problem persists under \(N\ge1\) and \(Y=0\). Intermediate counter
transformations matter; the static source zero-run bound is insufficient.

A separate 201-subtree reassociation had a seven-zero source run and
poor allocation compatibility. Some pure decoder rotations created
identical rows but broke a context-sensitive arithmetic entrance. They
failed the full runtime check and are not accepted machines. An inductive
source-value analysis excluded five otherwise generic symbolic cases but
left every literal row needed elsewhere, giving no physical saving.

The bounded search on U214 considered 45,369 simple state quotients,
437,928 one-row candidates, and 7,147,428 two-row candidates, with
radius-four abstract contexts and rendezvous paths up to 31 steps.
It found no further accepted reduction. These statistics are not a lower
bound. Equivalent slower paths and larger accepted alternatives were
not selected over the simpler primary table.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Can the role reassignment and its coincident-source/output case be
formalized directly in the existing PA/MM0 numerical-calculus development,
then composed with a literal U214 endpoint? The unchanged logic templates
and exact macro bindings isolate the new work.
\item Can physical allocation optimize for a subsequent guarded fold?
The allocator left a context-specific state that the local proof removes;
incorporating that condition may expose another saving.
\item How much more can joint optimization of selector roles, binary
parenthesization and physical tape contexts achieve? Instruction count
and source-DAG size alone are insufficient objectives.
\item Can two-sided local convergence become a routine compiler proof
rule? The direct 217-state reduction compares five old steps with three
new ones in one branch, beyond one-old-step simulation searches.
\item What is the sharp zero-run bound throughout every intermediate
program-counter transformation? A proved bound could permit a smaller
detector; blank-start success and the static source bound do not settle it.
\item Do relational register invariants, or another equally strong
covering bundle, remove a physical state while retaining a short proof?
\end{enumerate}

\begin{abstract}
We compare all eight supplied 213-state proposals and construct an explicit
\textbf{212-working-state, two-symbol, single-tape Turing machine}, including
its blank-tape initializer. The successful combination uses the
direct-transfer source and seven-zero origin detector of proposal B, and
the entry-bypass argument of proposal H. The essential adaptation is to
translate H's helper state 167 to state 211 in B's different allocation.
Two retained transition rows change, native state 112 is deleted, and the
source program is unchanged. Four universal, tape-preserving path
identities prove halting equivalence with the exact 213-state parent.
For every halting computation from the common start, the new time is at
most the old time, and the old time is at most $7/3$ of the new time.
The complete 48,140-step calibrated blank prefix is unchanged. A fresh
unary/list-inductive runtime replay discharges all 5,084 guarded primitive
contracts and covers all 424 final transition rows. Composing the new
PA-formalizable machine equivalence with the retained parent calibration
gives $\PA\vdash\neg\Halt(U_{212},\blank)\leftrightarrow\Con(\PA)$.
The endpoint uses the explicitly identified ordinary mathematical
calibration; no new end-to-end proof-assistant certificate is asserted.
\end{abstract}

\begin{theorem}[Literal-machine preservation]\label{thm:main}
From state 0 and the same initial binary tape, $P$ halts if and only if
$Q$ halts. The result is formalizable in PA for arithmetically coded
tapes and finite computations; in particular,
\[
 \PA\vdash\Halt(P,\blank)\longleftrightarrow\Halt(Q,\blank).
\]
If the common computation halts and $T_P,T_Q$ are its literal transition
counts, then
\[
                 T_Q\le T_P\le\frac73T_Q.
\]
\end{theorem}
The preservation theorem is independent of the correctness of the
inherited arithmetic calibration. Section~\ref{sec:logical-calibration}
states the additional dependencies used for the consistency corollary.

\section{The bypass: three universal path identities}\label{sec:bypass}
Let $J$ be the 213-state intermediate obtained from $P$ by changing only
$180/1$ to $(1,R,211)$. All other 425 rows agree. Use $(q,h)$ for the
state and relative head coordinate, set the entry coordinate to zero,
and let $\tau$ be an arbitrary binary tape. At the exceptional entry,
$\tau(0)=1$.

In each case, both computations finish in exactly the same state, at
the same head coordinate, with the same \emph{entire tape}. Indeed every
displayed write preserves the scanned bit. The first case inspects only
coordinates 0 and 1; the other two inspect only 0, 1, and 2. The rest of
the tape is arbitrary and untouched. No interior state is halt. These
three patterns exhaust all possible tapes at state 180 scanning one.
\section{Strengthened entry information removes state 112}

The complete incoming-edge inventory of native 172 in $P$ is
\[
       (116,0)\mapsto(0,R,172),\qquad
       (180,1)\mapsto(1,R,172).
\]
After the bypass, only the first of these remains in $J$.
Since the initial state is zero, every subsequent entry to 172 in $J$
therefore has a zero immediately to the left of the head. The complete
incoming inventory of native 112 is
\[
                       (172,0)\mapsto(0,L,112).
\]

At state 172 with head coordinate zero, the applicable condition is
$(\tau(-1),\tau(0))=(0,0)$. The fourth matching identity is
\begin{align*}
 J:\quad &(172,0)\to(112,-1)\to(157,0)\to(67,-1)\to(151,0),\\
 Q:\quad &(172,0)\to(67,-1)\to(151,0).
\end{align*}
Both paths leave the whole tape unchanged and inspect only the two stated
zero cells. The lengths are four and two. Redirecting $172/0$ to 67 now
leaves no incoming edge to 112, so both rows of 112 can be deleted.
All other rows of $J$ and $Q$ agree.

The order of the two edits is essential to this proof. In the original
$P$, the entry from $180/1$ writes a one immediately left of 172, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:zeros} would be false if asserted before that entry was
bypassed. Nor is this a claim that states 112 and 67 have the same behavior
on arbitrary configurations.

\subsection{A direct synchronized-checkpoint proof}
One can compare $P$ and $Q$ directly without making an intermediate run
part of the theorem statement. Start at the common initial configuration.
At each checkpoint, both computations have identical state, head, and
whole tape. Use a case from Section~\ref{sec:bypass} whenever the state is
180 and the scanned bit is one. Those matching blocks end at 184, 90,
or 86, so they never end at 172 or 112. At state 172 scanning zero, use
the four-step/two-step identity. Every other checkpoint uses the common
one-step transition.

Maintain two checkpoint properties: the state is not 112; and a checkpoint
at 172 has zero immediately to its left. Both hold initially. The only
ordinary transition into 172 is $116/0$, since $180/1$ is handled inside
its own block; $116/0$ establishes the required zero. The only ordinary
way to enter 112 would be $172/0$, which is likewise handled inside the
fourth block. None of the exceptional block endpoints is 112 or 172.
Thus the invariant is preserved, and every stated block is applicable.

\subsection{Arithmetization}
For a PA statement, encode finite-support initial tapes and finite run
histories by natural numbers. The blank tape has a fixed code. All row
lookups, local tape restrictions, finite transition checks, and block
choices are primitive recursive. The checkpoint invariant is proved by
induction on the number of blocks. Given a halting trace, primitive
recursion parses successive positive blocks and emits the matching trace;
the explicit finite bound on block lengths proves termination of this
translation in PA. Its inverse uses the same four identities. This is
a PA-formalizable proof of literal halting equivalence and requires no
consistency assumption.

The ordinary mathematical simulation also applies to arbitrary initial
binary tapes. This broader statement is not confused with a first-order
PA quantification over arbitrary uncoded functions $\mathbb Z\to\{0,1\}$.
The arithmetical consistency endpoint uses the fixed blank input only.

The pairs of old/new block lengths are
\[
                     (1,1),\quad(2,2),\quad(7,3),\quad(4,2).
\]
Let $r$ count the seven-step bypass blocks and $s$ count the four-step
two-zero blocks in the common checkpoint sequence of a halting run. Then
\[
                        T_P-T_Q=4r+2s.
\]
Every new block is no longer than the corresponding old block, and the
largest ratio of old to new lengths is $7/3$. Summation yields

it does not assert that the blank computation halts. A time saving need
not be strict on every input, while the working-state saving is exactly one.

uses the already available induction with ambient parameters; old graph
objects are bound in the comprehension formulas. Addition, multiplication,
and the translated PA induction schema result.

For every common initial tape and head position, runs of $R$ and $M$ from

\subsection{The offset simulation principle}
For a deleted state $q$ represented by $r$ at offset $k$, use the boundary map
$F(q,h,T)=(r,h+k,T)$ and $F(s,h,T)=(s,h,T)$ otherwise. An ordinary retained
row entering $q$ changes its displacement from $d$ to $d+k$; legality requires
$d+k\in\{-1,1\}$. At $k=\pm2$, all such entrances must point the opposite
way. If every exceptional row has a positive, nonhalting, complete-tape macro
to the image of its old successor, induction proves halting equivalence just
as in Theorem~4.1. For $q=0$, translating the homogeneous blank tape permits
initial head 0, but every later runtime occurrence of $q$ still needs its
macro proof. No successful offset candidate is claimed.

\subsection{Open constructive routes}
Three precise extensions remain open; none is promised to save a state.
First, the dead-loop deletion needs new sharing or allocation, since the fixed
AST edit costs three DAG nodes. Second, simulation boundaries could permit
controlled tape differences or phase-dependent offsets, beyond the present
complete-tape and constant-offset templates. Third, a richer source-boundary
guard domain could preserve correlations lost in seven- and nine-bit windows,
especially inside the 25 conservatively opaque engine states.

Any advance must supply an actual total table of at most 207 working states,
including initialization, with a sound boundary invariant, progress and halt
reflection, and the retained proof-search calibration. A new table requires

\begin{theorem}[Uniform preservation of halting]
\label{thm:all-tape}
From state 0, the exact principal U209 and U208 tables halt on exactly
the same initial binary tapes. At matching points their tapes and head
positions agree. If the old computation halts after \(n\) steps, the new
one halts after
\[
\tau(n)=n+6A(n)+2B(n),
\]
where \(A(n)\) counts old 172/read-0 transitions and \(B(n)\) counts old
211/read-0 transitions among those \(n\) steps. In particular,
\(n\le\tau(n)\le7n\).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The initial configurations satisfy \(\mathcal R\), because \(\rho(0)=0\).
Induct on the number of old steps. In an ordinary state, the single new
step commutes with \(\rho\). In states 172 and 211, the old-machine
lemmas supply the relevant guards, and the appropriate block in
Table~\ref{tab:cases} returns to \(\mathcal R\). Summing the block
lengths gives the stated clock formula. All block lengths are positive.

If the old computation halts, the constructed finite new computation
reaches the corresponding halt. Conversely suppose the new machine
halts at time \(T\). If the old machine did not halt in its first \(T\)
steps, the induction would construct a new computation through
\(\tau(T)\ge T\) whose synchronized endpoints are working states and
whose internal blocks contain no halt. This contradicts halting at time
\(T\). Hence the old computation also halts.
\end{proof}

There is no circularity in the internal revisits to new 211 and new 163.
The lemmas concern only the old machine at old-step boundaries. The
seven-step new trace is executed directly, including the new 211/read-0
row on its second use. We do not assert the old invariant at each
transient configuration of the new machine.

The supplied unary manuscript~\cite{incoming} uses classical equality-free first-order
logic on nonempty domains, with one binary predicate \(E\). Write
\[
\Sub(x,a):=\forall z\,(E(z,x)\to E(z,a)).
\]
For each formula \(\varphi\) with free variables contained in \(\{x\}\),
the theory U contains
\[
\forall a\,\exists b\left[
\forall x\,(E(x,b)\to\varphi(x))\ \land\
\forall x\,(\Sub(x,a)\to(\varphi(x)\to E(x,b)))\right].
\tag{U}
\]
The source parameter \(a\) is not allowed free in \(\varphi\).
There is no bound on bound-variable count, formula size, or quantifier
complexity. No extensionality axiom is assumed. In particular, replacing
\(\varphi(x)\) by \(\Sub(x,a)\land\psi(x)\) would violate the stated
unary restriction, so ordinary unrestricted separation cannot simply be
inserted into the lower interpretation.

\subsection{Why the retained U/PA proof is substantive}
The supplied unary manuscript~\cite{unary} contains a detailed ordinary
interpretation argument. Its upper direction interprets membership as binary
bit membership in PA. Bit inclusion implies \(x\le a\); for each fixed
arithmetical matrix, PA's induction constructs the finite characteristic code
on the interval through \(a\). This is formula-specific finite comprehension,
not a uniform truth predicate, and works inside arbitrary PA models.

For the lower direction, equality is interpreted by coextensionality.
The numerical representatives explicitly include saturation and suitable
first-order order/endpoint conditions. Local predecessor facts establish
induction before total successor existence is used. Comparison and least
failing numerical tuples then allow parameters to be bound inside a legal
unary matrix. Bounded numerical comprehension follows, with its support and
invariance premises stated explicitly. This provides successors, numerical
powers, pair and graph codes, and canonical finite histories for addition and
multiplication. The order of these steps avoids a circular appeal to total
successors.

This distinction is essential. The separate positive dyadic emitter in the
unary-theory ZIP is not the program implemented by these U211, U210, or U209
tables. Its operation counts cannot be used as a runtime or state-count
certificate for them.

\section{The bypass and its three universal paths}
Only $180/1$ differs between $A$ and $B$. At a configuration with state
180 and scanned symbol 1, take the head position as coordinate 0 and
write $b$ for cell 1. When $b=0$, write $c$ for cell 2. All the following

relative head coordinate.

All other 427 rows agree between $A$ and $B$. Thus the runs can be

\section{Why the bypass permits a state deletion}
The original table has two incoming rows to 172: $116/0$ and $180/1$.
Their preceding symbols differ. After the bypass, $B$ has only
\[
 B(116,0)=(0,R,172).
\]
Consequently every visit to 172 on a run initially in state 0 has a zero
immediately left of the head. The only incoming row to 112 remains
\[
 B(172,0)=(0,L,112).
\]
On that step, the current zero becomes the cell right of the new head;
the previously established left zero becomes its scanned cell.

\begin{lemma}[Two zeros]
Whenever $B$, started in state 0, reaches state 112, both the scanned cell
and its immediate right neighbor contain zero.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Neither 172 nor 112 is the initial state. The two complete incoming-row
lists above show, by inspection of the last transition entering each
state, that 172 has a preceding zero and that its zero branch enters 112
on that preceding cell while leaving a zero to its right. The first
statement is an invariant of every finite run from state 0, so it applies
at each such predecessor. No assumption about the initial tape is used.
\end{proof}

At state 112, use the invariant and take the head coordinate as zero:
\begin{align*}
 B:\quad &(112,0)\to(157,1)\to(67,0)\to(151,1),\\
 C:\quad &(67,0)\to(151,1).
\end{align*}
Both paths preserve cells 0 and 1, both zero, and inspect no exterior
cell. The former has three steps, the latter one. This is the fourth
universal local identity.

Map $112\mapsto67$ and fix every other native label, including halt.
The final table deletes 112 and redirects its incoming target under this
map. All 426 other old rows commute with the map. At 112 the displayed
three-to-one identity supplies the exceptional block. Alternatively,
start the comparison one step earlier at $172/0$: the old four-step and
new two-step paths both end in state 151 at the original head coordinate.
The independent checker uses this latter equal-state formulation.

\section{PA formalization and the runtime comparison}
For each stage, build a common sequence of synchronized configurations.
Every block has positive length, finite explicitly bounded length, and
no halt in its interior. The two machines agree on halting at the common
endpoints; in the second stage the state map fixes halt and takes no
working state to halt. Determinism identifies each displayed block with
the actual execution prefix.

To prove either implication, induct on the length of a given finite
halting trace. The zero-length case is immediate. Otherwise remove the
appropriate positive block; it cannot cross a halt in its interior.
Apply the induction hypothesis at its matching endpoint and prefix the
other machine's block. This proves equivalence without an assumption of
consistency or of infinite execution. Primitive recursive coding of finite
tapes and execution sequences, verification of the fixed identities, and
natural-number induction formalize this reasoning in PA. The marker
argument is itself an induction on finite execution length.

Every new block is no longer than its old counterpart. If $r$ counts the
seven-step exceptional bypass blocks in the old $A$ execution, and $s$
counts visits to 112 in the corresponding intermediate $B$ execution,
then, whenever halting occurs,
\[
 T_B=T_A-4r,\qquad T_C=T_B-2s,\qquad T_C=T_A-4r-2s.
\]
The counts belong to the stated \emph{different} executions; both are
finite, nonnegative integers. The formulas do not claim that all programs
or all inputs get a strict speedup, nor that the actual blank machine
halts. They give weak literal-time dominance on any halting execution.

\paragraph{A sharper direct comparison.}
One may synchronize $A$ directly with $C$ at equal-state checkpoints,
never choosing 112 as a checkpoint. At such checkpoints, state 172 has
zero to its left: its only ordinary incoming row is $116/0$, while
$180/1$ is handled inside the three bypass blocks. Those blocks end in
184, 90, or 86, and cannot create a checkpoint at 172. The $172/0$ block
has four old steps and two new steps, ending at state 151 at the original
head coordinate. All remaining blocks have lengths one and one.
The block ratios are therefore $1$, $7/3$, or $2$. Summing along any
finite halting run proves the stronger bound
\[
             T_C\le T_A\le \tfrac{7}{3}T_C.
\]
This is a checkpoint invariant, not a claim that every original visit
to 172 has a preceding zero. The time result applies in particular to
the blank tape, conditionally on halting, and to arithmetically coded
common initial tapes.

\paragraph{Two-way halting preservation.}
Relate configurations with identical tape and head by the identity on
states other than 167, and relate an old state-167 configuration to the
corresponding new state-172 configuration under the established
preceding-one guard.  At an ordinary checkpoint the same single transition
is executed, except that an old destination 167 is replaced by 172 and
establishes the guard.  At an exceptional checkpoint use the displayed
one/one or two/six block.  These blocks have positive lengths on both
sides and have no internal halt.  Induction on the successive checkpoints
therefore produces the entire run on each side, including any final halt.
An infinite run on one side yields infinitely many checkpoints and hence
an infinite run on the other.  Consequently the two machines halt
equivalently from every common initial tape in state 0.
If a common halt occurs after $t$ old steps and $s$ new steps, these
particular block alignments give the explicit bound
\[
                         t\leq s\leq 3t.
\]
Thus both finite run translations have elementary numerical bounds;
the local compression trades extra running time for one fewer state.

This argument uses finite transition identities and induction on finite

in particular the blank tape, is provable in PA.  The new machine inherits

\section{A numerical proof of equivalence of the full axiom bundles}
\label{sec:logical}

The source section defines $H_{214}$ and $H_{213}$. The full enabled
numerical bundles also contain the unchanged vacuity term
\[
 V=I\bigl(R(a,b),Q(c,R(a,b))\bigr),\qquad
 B_{214}=N(I(V,H_{214})),\quad B_{213}=N(I(V,H_{213})).
\]
The gate remains $c\ne a\land c\ne b$; a disabled selector emits the
same truth code zero. It is therefore sufficient to prove both bundle
implications uniformly in all three numerical selectors.

\begin{proposition}[Uniform bundle exchange]
For arbitrary natural $a,b,c$, the common numerical logical calculus
derives $I(B_{214},B_{213})$ and $I(B_{213},B_{214})$ without additional
hypotheses or selector restrictions.
\end{proposition}

If $X\to Y$ is a theorem, unrestricted generalization and the retained
quantifier-distribution schema $\rho_2$ give
$Q(v,X)\to Q(v,Y)$. The same implication rules give the two operations
\[
 (X\to Y)\ \Longrightarrow\ ((U\to X)\to(U\to Y)),\qquad
 (X\to Y)\ \Longrightarrow\ ((Y\to F)\to(X\to F)),
\]
where the inherited falsity code is $F=1$.
Starting with exchange at $(A,B,C)=(a,G,E)$, first lift through $Q(c,-)$.
Use the second operation for negation, the first for antecedent $U$,
then lift through $Q(a,-)$, use antecedent $V$, and negate once more.
The two contravariant operations restore the original orientation,
giving $B_{214}\to B_{213}$. Start from the converse exchange to obtain
$B_{213}\to B_{214}$.

\section{Rejected shortcuts and boundaries of the result}

The investigation retained failures that distinguish a genuine runtime
argument from an attractive state count.

\paragraph{Shortening the zero return scan.}
Bypassing state 50 after state 34 gives a 213-state table and even reaches
a calibrated-looking blank frame after 86,828 transitions. Nevertheless
the full primitive proof fails at ordinal 26, the zero branch of
\texttt{CD1} at address \texttt{1101001001000000}. The maximum zero run
of the static source is six, but intermediate return processing changes
the relevant patterns. Static address metrics and a successful blank
prefix are insufficient to justify this shortcut.

\paragraph{Source-preserving reallocation and a valid local fold.}
A different 214-state reallocation preserves U214's source and creates
a two-zero predecessor invariant. Under that invariant a path through
native 112 can indeed be replaced by an existing two-step path through
7. A finite whole-tape certificate proves this local 214-to-213 quotient.
The intermediate allocation, however, used a source-entry state under
the wrong preceding bit. An earlier version also reassigned arithmetic
rows omitted from an inherited protection filter. The valid local fold
does not repair the invalid intermediate interpreter. That route is
recorded as rejected research, not as a second accepted U213.

\paragraph{A context error in the successful source family.}
The first allocation of the delivered source used state 150 after a
preceding zero at one relation-constructor entry. A concrete valid
register frame demonstrated the wrong result, despite successful decoder
prefix and blank-start checks. The final table instead uses state 182
under its proved preceding-zero condition, with its helper rows retained.
The complete table was then rechecked; a local repair by itself was not
treated as global acceptance.

The accepted result is one explicit 213-state construction. No accepted
212-state construction was obtained. The finite allocation searches and
failed local folds establish no lower bound for arbitrary machines.
Promising next steps are to include predecessor-bit conditions directly
in allocation constraints and to optimize allocation together with
guarded state deletion. A separate task is to export this exact table,
runtime derivations, and inherited logical calibration into one checked
proof-assistant endpoint.

\subsection{The incoming tape bit provides the missing distinction}

The complete incoming-edge inventories of the two relevant states are
\[
 \delta_R(188,1)=(1,R,211),\qquad
 \delta_R(181,0)=(0,R,214).
\]
There are no other entrances to either state. Neither is initial. Hence
every run from state zero satisfies the inductive invariant
\begin{equation}\label{eq:invariant}
 \mathcal I(q,h,t):\Longleftrightarrow
 (q=211\Rightarrow t(h-1)=1)\ \land\
 (q=214\Rightarrow t(h-1)=0).
\end{equation}
This holds on every initial binary tape, not only on the blank tape.
It follows directly from the most recent transition that enters the state.

The two states have the same read-one behavior and different read-zero
behavior:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
q&\delta_R(q,0)&\delta_R(q,1)\\\hline
211&(0,R,90)&(1,R,218)\\
214&(0,R,98)&(1,R,218).
\end{array}
\]
Existing states already contain the selector and exits needed to recover
the distinction from the preceding tape bit:
\[
 \delta_R(155,0)=(0,R,85),\quad
 \delta_R(155,1)=(1,R,150),\quad
 \delta_R(85,0)=(0,R,98),\quad
 \delta_R(150,0)=(0,R,90).
\]

Define \(\pi(214)=211\), and \(\pi(q)=q\) for every other state,
including halt. Delete state 214, redirect its incoming target to 211,
and replace the representative's zero row by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:changedrow}
                         \delta_N(211,0)=(0,L,155).
\end{equation}
Every other retained row is the old row with its target renamed by
\(\pi\). Thus the final fold itself changes two retained rows and
deletes two rows; the remaining changes relative to U214 are the rotations.

For scanned one, both old states take the same one-step transition to
218, and U213 does the same. For scanned zero, start the head at \(h\).
Equation~\eqref{eq:changedrow} moves to \(h-1\) in state 155. The
following two steps select the correct exit:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{old state and tag}&\text{new state path}&\text{endpoint}\\\hline
211,\ t(h-1)=1&211\to155\to150\to90&(90,h+1,t)\\
214,\ t(h-1)=0&211\to155\to85\to98&(98,h+1,t).
\end{array}
\]
Every write restores the symbol already present. Only cells \(h-1\)
and \(h\) are read, and all other cells are untouched. The complete
tape and head position at the endpoint equal those of the corresponding
old single step. Neither path passes through halt internally.

\begin{theorem}[Local fold, arbitrary initial tape]
\label{thm:local}
Starting in state zero on any binary tape, \(R_{214}\) and U213 halt
equivalently. If an old prefix has \(n\) transitions and contains
\(N_0\) visits to states 211 or 214 scanning zero, its corresponding
new prefix has exactly
\[
                        m=n+2N_0,
             \qquad n\le m\le 3n.
\]
The statement and its blank-tape instance are formalizable in PA.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The invariant~\eqref{eq:invariant} is true initially and is preserved
by every old transition. At a configuration satisfying it, each old step
has either a one-step or a three-step new simulation. The endpoints have
the same tape and head, with control state projected by \(\pi\).
Concatenating these positive-duration blocks proves preservation and
the exact time formula. There is no internal halt in any block.

The independent fold checker reads the two tables directly and imports

simulations and four three-step simulations. The exterior is opaque:
an attempted read outside the represented cells is rejected. Thus each
successful endpoint equality applies to every extension of the local
frame to an entire tape.

induction on the arbitrary run length. A traversal of the remaining
spare list is justified by structural induction after its exact generic
one-block schema has been rederived from the table. All four such
schemas are rederived. Affine expressions record elapsed time and head
displacement, and every completed primitive has strictly positive
duration. A nonhalting primitive reaches its specified successor frame;
the halt primitive reaches native halt 254.

\section{The retained consistency interpretation}\label{sec:logic}

The unary theory \(\ThU\) has one binary relation and no equality,
constants, or function symbols. Put
\(\Sub(x,s):=\forall z(E(z,x)\to E(z,s))\).
For every matrix \(\varphi(x)\) with no free variable other than \(x\),
its schema asserts
\[
 \forall s\,\exists C\,\forall x\,
 \bigl[(E(x,C)\to\varphi(x))\land

\section{A preceding symbol replaces one decoder state}\label{sec:fold}

The rotations expose two states with the same action on one but different
actions on zero. In \(\Rot\), the relevant literal rows are

\text{native state} & \text{read }0 & \text{read }1\\\hline
214 & (0,R,98) & (1,R,218)\\
115 & (0,R,90) & (1,R,218)\\
155 & (0,R,85) & (1,R,150)\\
85  & (0,R,98) & \text{not used in the fold}\\
150 & (0,R,90) & \text{not used in the fold}
\end{array}
\]
Every incoming transition to state 214 is the single row
\(\delta(181,0)=(0,R,214)\). Every incoming transition to state 115 is
\(\delta(167,1)=(1,R,115)\). Hence in every run starting at state zero,
\[
 q=214\Longrightarrow T(h-1)=0,\qquad
 q=115\Longrightarrow T(h-1)=1.                     \tag{1}
\]
This invariant holds for any initial tape, not just the blank tape.
It is initially vacuous and follows at each subsequent entry from the
symbol just written and the rightward move.

Delete native state 115, redirect its incoming target to 214, and replace
only the zero row of the retained state by
\[
                  \delta'(214,0)=(0,L,155).          \tag{2}
\]
All other retained rows are unchanged. Let \(\rho(115)=214\), with
\(\rho\) the identity on every other state, including halt. The state
number in the invariant distinguishes two old cases; the preceding tape
bit remembers that distinction in the merged machine.

\begin{lemma}[Whole-tape fold]\label{lem:fold}
If an old configuration satisfies (1), its one-step successor is simulated
under \(\rho\) by one or three steps of the new machine, with identical
head position and entire tape at the endpoint. The simulating block has
positive duration and does not visit halt internally.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For states other than 214 and 115, the old row and new row agree after
renaming their targets, so one step suffices. If either exceptional state
reads one, its old row and the merged row both write one, move right and
enter state 218.

Suppose the scanned cell at position \(h\) contains zero. Let
\(b=T(h-1)\). Equation (2) preserves the zero and moves to \(h-1\).
State 155 preserves \(b\) and moves back to \(h\), entering state 85
if \(b=0\), or state 150 if \(b=1\). These states read the preserved
zero and perform respectively the old zero action of 214 or of 115.
The invariant supplies the correct value of \(b\). Both cells are
restored, the final head is \(h+1\), and the final state is respectively
98 or 90. No other cell is read or written. Thus an arbitrary tape
exterior is preserved, and the block has exactly three nonhalting steps.
\end{proof}

For the converse, the deterministic new run is partitioned by these
positive blocks. If the old run never halts, the synchronizing times are
unbounded, and the nonhalting blocks cover every finite new time. No
new halt can be hidden inside a block. Equivalently, a finite alleged new
halting time is covered by a finite number of old steps and contradicts
either a nonhalting endpoint or the interior-block check. This is the
required halt reflection, not merely a one-way simulation.
\end{proof}

A radius-two exhaustive check can enumerate all five-cell frames, keeping

(1): each exceptional state excludes sixteen frames. Sixteen admitted
frames use three new steps; every other admitted frame uses one. The
checker also verifies preservation of the old invariant, the complete
endpoint tape, and the absence of any opaque-exterior read. Mutating an
entry tag, a helper branch, or the new write gives negative controls.
This small certificate is independent of the numerical-calculus logic.

halting trace. The zero-length case is immediate. Otherwise remove the
appropriate positive block; it cannot cross a halt in its interior.

consistency or of infinite execution. Primitive recursive coding of finite

necessary nor correct to assume that every intermediate visit of the

The original question asked for a machine with fewer than 209 states, after
comparing several constructions based on the proposed unary theory $\UU$.
The subsequently supplied commits already contain 208-state constructions.
The research target of this dossier is therefore \textbf{at most 207 working
states}. Reproducing a supplied U208 construction does not meet that revised
target, and a state renaming does not constitute a further saving.

Throughout, a machine has one two-way infinite tape, alphabet $\{0,1\}$,
blank symbol 0, head coordinate 0 at initialization, and an all-zero initial
tape. Every transition writes one symbol and moves exactly one position
left or right. The halt label is separate and is not a working state.
Initialization counts. Sparse native labels such as 211 or 302 are names;
they do not indicate the number of states. A row
\[
 q\quad b\quad w\quad D\quad r
\]
means: in state $q$ scanning $b$, write $w$, move in direction $D$, and enter
$r$. Entry into the halt label halts after the write and move.

An acceptable additional saving needs more than a syntactically shorter
source program or a finite blank-tape run. The intended endpoint is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:endpoint}
 \PA\vdash\neg\Halt(M,\mathrm{blank})\ \longleftrightarrow\ \Con(\PA).
\end{equation}
A local reduction can establish this by proving, within PA, equivalence
with an already calibrated parent. A changed source program instead needs
a source-level soundness and completeness argument, the corresponding
literal machine implementation, and a valid blank initialization. The
distinction matters because source decoding and arithmetic operations share
physical states in these compact machines.

The archive distinguishes four levels of evidence:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Exact finite data}: table totality, target closure, state count,
renaming, hashes, and rooted graph isomorphism.
\item \emph{Finite proof certificates}: bounded predecessor invariants and
whole-tape local simulation identities, or inductive symbolic runtime
contracts with arbitrary natural-number parameters.
\item \emph{Inherited mathematical calibration}: enumeration of the native
calculus and its consistency equivalence with $\UU$ and PA.
\item \emph{Proof-assistant certification}: a final theorem checked in a
kernel against the exact table and exact theory specifications.
\end{enumerate}
The supplied U208 packets and this work provide evidence at the first three
levels, with different portions newly checked here. They do not export a
new end-to-end PA, Lean, Rocq, or MM0 proof object for a smaller U machine.

Halting reflection can be expressed without infinite objects: if the child

The proposed theory $\UU$ uses an equality-free membership language. For
each formula $\varphi(x)$ with no other free variable, it contains
\begin{equation}\label{eq:U}
\forall a\,\exists b\left[
 \forall x\bigl(x\in b\to\varphi(x)\bigr)\ \land\
 \forall x\bigl(\Sub(x,a)\to(\varphi(x)\to x\in b)\bigr)\right],
\end{equation}
where $\Sub(x,a)$ abbreviates
$\forall z(z\in x\to z\in a)$. This is weak covering: the selected
subsets of $a$ must be included, and all members of $b$ satisfy the matrix.
It is not an unrestricted exact separation axiom with arbitrary parameters.
The distinction is central to the claimed minimality of the theory
\cite{unary}.

The unary archive gives an ordinary mathematical argument for proof-code
translations in both directions between the appropriate consistency
statements. The lower interpretation needs more than a sentence saying
``finite ordinals exist.'' In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Equality is represented by equality of member profiles. Substitution
in the member position requires saturated containing objects; it is not
automatic from the definition of coextensionality.
\item Numerical representatives have internal order and predecessor
properties. Induction is established before successor totality, so that
successors are not silently assumed while proving them.
\item Parameter induction is obtained by using the genuinely unary matrix
$Q(v)=\forall\vec p(A_\theta(\vec p)\to\theta(v,\vec p))$, where
$A_\theta$ expresses the base and step premises.
\item Least failed numerical tuples are bound inside unary formulas to
obtain bounded numerical comprehension with its support condition. This
does not introduce a uniform truth predicate.
\item Successors, powers of numerical sources, pair codes, and canonical
graphs for addition and multiplication are built only after the required
induction and comprehension statements.
\end{enumerate}
The inspected proof supplies these dependencies. This audit found no
concrete parameter violation or circularity in those steps. It does not
replace them by a newly implemented general proof translator.

For the upper interpretation, use $x\in a$ as the bit predicate
$\operatorname{Bit}(a,x)$. Translated subsethood bounds the possible $x$;
formula-specific PA induction forms the required finite collection. This
is compatible with unbounded formula complexity because a separate PA
proof is produced for each fixed formula.

The actual U209/U208 source retains a four-tag numerical calculus. With
the constructor used by the code,
\[
P(x,y)=\frac{(x+y)(x+y+1)}2+y,
\]
its tags are implication $4P$, membership $4P+1$, quantification $4P+2$,
and auxiliary equality $4P+3$. Code 0 is a normalized closed truth alias;
target code 1 is diagonal membership, interpreted as false under global
irreflexivity. The pairing convention must be taken from the executable
constructor, rather than guessed from the phrase ``dual Cantor pairing.''

The separate positive dyadic stream in the unary archive uses different
tags and target code 0. It is an alternative design, not the backend of

None of those statements proves that 208 is minimal. State counts are the
end of a chain of choices: axioms, formula coding, enumeration program,
source association, contextual allocation, tape representation, and local
machine reductions. A negative result at one level does not bound the
other levels. Nor does a broad heuristic search establish that an
unexamined configuration relation cannot save a state.

The search code therefore records assumptions, bounds, and positive controls
alongside outcomes. A generated table that lacks a proof of its intended
behavior is kept in rejected research data rather than silently promoted
to a consistency machine. The requested construction with at most 207
working states remains unresolved in this investigation.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Can source layout and helper behavior be synthesized together?}
The repeated grammar failure shows that a state should carry a family of
entry contracts, including backward arithmetic entries. An allocator could
optimize these contracts jointly with source association instead of first
optimizing a pure decoder and later discovering the conflict.
\item \textbf{Can the configuration relation change economically?}
Two machines need not synchronize after every old transition with identical
head coordinates and tape. Small fixed head offsets, temporary marker
changes, or synchronization at source boundaries may permit reductions
excluded by the present local search. The associated proof should establish
positive progress and halting reflection explicitly.
\item \textbf{Can the all-spares-one invariant replace a generic list engine?}
A proof specialized to fixed spare blocks might permit a shorter scanner
or delimiter mechanism while leaving the primary registers unbounded.
The whole initialization and append invariant must remain part of the
theorem.
\item \textbf{Can axiom-builder order and association outperform parameter
permutations?} The 279,936-case result fixes association. Reordering complete
builders preserves the emitted axiom set, but interacts with scratch-state
reuse and the protected-tail argument. A physical saving needs a measured
allocation and final runtime proof.
\item \textbf{Can the positive dyadic calculus be compiled completely?}
Its alternative syntax may simplify formula construction, but the full cost
includes proof enumeration, vacuity/freshness handling, substitution if used,
and blank initialization. Comparing only formula sizes is inconclusive.
\item \textbf{Can the U/PA calibration be turned into an explicit proof
translator?} A proof-code implementation would separate the mathematical
strength question from changes to the machine backend and would provide a
clear target for the MM0 or other small-kernel route.
\end{enumerate}

Why the source equality is sufficient
------------------------------------
Both sources have configurations (i,r), with i the ordinal instruction index
and r the nine natural-number registers. Increments, decrements, jumps, and
halt are interpreted by their resolved ordinal rows. Equality of every row
therefore makes their one-step transition functions identical for every
configuration, including both zero and positive decrement outcomes. Induction
on any finite run length yields identical source runs and identical halting
behavior, from the seed or from any other ordinal configuration. The source
paths differ; the register semantics do not.

\begin{lemma}[Positive total segments permit bounded reversal]
Let a deterministic source program have a primitive-recursive totalized
step function, with a distinguished halting instruction, and let the

\begin{theorem}[All-tape positive-block simulation]\label{thm:fold}
Start $P$ and $M$ in state 0 with the same tape and head coordinate. At
matched boundaries the head and entire tape agree, and the child state is

same halting behavior from every such common initial configuration.

\subsection{Unary U and its PA interpretation}

bounds the candidate elements, and formula-specific finite comprehension

not evaluate a general truth predicate.

The lower interpretation uses numerical representatives modulo
coextensionality, with saturation providing the needed membership
congruence. Its construction order is consequential: local predecessor
facts first give induction without total successors; comparison and least
numerical failures then give bounded numerical comprehension with the
parameters bound inside legal unary matrices. Total successors, numerical
powers, saturated ordered-pair codes, and canonical bounded histories
follow. Addition and multiplication are defined by those histories, and
translated PA induction uses the earlier induction theorem.

Our reading found no concrete illicit free parameter or circular successor
assumption in those examined steps. The package supplies ordinary
mathematical proof templates, not an implemented general translator for
arbitrary PA proofs or a kernel certificate. We retain that scope rather
than presenting finite diagnostics as a new proof of equiconsistency.

The U209 machine does not implement a unary-free-variable validator. Its
inherited numerical calculus is calibrated to unrestricted weak covering
$\W$, allowing additional matrix parameters, together with global
irreflexivity. Unary U embeds into this theory; the binary-membership
interpretation in PA validates the additional instances and irreflexivity.
These interpretations bridge the consistency presentations.

A structural search suggested reassociating
\[

Afterward states 85 and 154 have identical rows, apparently saving one
state by sharing the suffix $(12,150)$. The final identical-row quotient is
valid; the preceding rotation is not justified.

The reason is hidden reuse through backward execution. A purely rightward
source traversal sees three occurrences of 155. Full literal prefix
analysis finds five occurrences of 155 and ten bindings to 85, including
five not under those 155 roots. One such path is
\[
76\to152\to159\to118\to155\to85.
\]
It revisits already consumed bits. The exact source prefix
\texttt{0011001000001}, with a preceding one, exposes the failure: the old
machine completes at state 42 and offset 13 without changing the tape;
the rotated machine reaches state 41 at offset 12 and overwrites a one
with zero. The counterexample is retained in
\path{research/rejected_rotation.json}. No machine from that failed route
is included as a candidate.

Another test attempted to delete native state 34 from the seven-zero origin
detector by redirecting $23/0$ directly to 75. All source-address six-zero
runs are terminal after trimming the suffix, which initially suggested a
six-zero detector might suffice. The actual runtime uses temporary markers,
so a static trimmed-address statistic is insufficient. The shortened table
already fails the first primitive's zero-decrement symbolic contract at
source address \texttt{000000}. This exploratory table is not delivered.

Both failed ideas were screened against the literal runtime before a state
saving was accepted. The delivered 208-state result is solely the
three-cell history fold proved in Section~\ref{sec:proof}.

\item \textbf{Can the generic fold theorem be formalized once?}
A proof-assistant library could accept a state projection, finite incoming
history covers, ordinary-row equations, and finite positive blocks, then
produce the blank-halting equivalence for a literal table. This would make
the incremental U209-to-U208 proof small. It would not by itself formalize
the separate numerical-calculus and U/PA interpretation layers.

\item \textbf{Can source sharing account for every physical decoder entry?}
The rejected rotation suggests enriching each source node with its complete
literal prefix interface, including known previously read bits and backward
entries. A transformation should transport those interfaces before counting
a shared suffix as a state saving.

\item \textbf{Do the two decoder allocations offer different next savings?}
Class B has a different 720-primitive address region and maximum depth 41.
The present history-fold mechanism also checks locally in its native
layout, with the appropriate helper names. The two layouts should remain
distinct search inputs rather than being counted as five independent designs.

No lower bound or global optimality assertion follows from this investigation.
The achieved result is an explicit, reproducible improvement from 209 to 208
working states with a small new halting-equivalence proof.

The lower interpretation avoids circularity in the following order:

The upper interpretation uses binary bit membership in PA. Inclusion of one-bit
sets bounds the subset code by the source; PA induction builds a characteristic
code for each fixed translated formula. This works formula by formula in
nonstandard PA models and does not invoke a uniform truth predicate. The same
interpretation satisfies unrestricted weak cover and global irreflexivity.

The stated finite-proof translations use primitive recursive syntax operations
and fixed proof templates. This supports the conventional internal theorem
`PA proves Con(U) iff Con(PA)`. There is no delivered general proof-translator
implementation or new Lean/Rocq/MM0 certificate for that unbounded theorem.

* A literal step requires a run length with constant term at least one, so it
  never guesses the first bit of a possibly empty unknown run.
* A self-loop that moves in the current direction consumes an arbitrary affine
  unary run in exactly its length, preserving the loop state. Its correctness
  is induction on that natural length, including zero.
* The four list-traversal lemmas are rederived from the exact transition table
  on a symbolic arbitrary block between opaque unread exteriors. Their duration
  and displacement are both checked as `v+2`. Finite-list induction composes them.
* The normalization identity `C(A) 1 = 1 B(A)` is valid for an empty list and
  follows for arbitrary finite lists from the one-block word identity.
  Reversal is handled explicitly. C and B blocks have the same length, so the
  single tail-width variable is preserved by every transformation used.
* Adjacent zero runs can be absorbed into an infinite blank exterior without
  changing the represented whole tape. Normalization preserves words.
* Each nonhalting primitive returns to the exact full-tape target key, not only
  register values. Expected address transformations and head displacement are
  checked separately. Halting primitives must reach the literal halt label.
* The returned duration has nonnegative affine coefficients and positive constant,
  so indefinitely composing source primitives cannot hide a zero-time loop.
