The supplied lower interpretation uses numerical representatives modulo
coextensionality, with saturation ensuring the required membership
congruence. Its dependency order matters. Local predecessor lemmas first
give induction without assuming successor totality. The induction proof
handles separately the case where no failure lies inside the given
numerical object. Quantifying the parameters of an induction assertion
inside its unary matrix then gives full parameterized representative
induction. Comparison and least numerical tuples provide bounded numerical
comprehension. Only afterward are successors, numerical powers, saturated
pair codes, and canonical finite histories obtained; iterating successor
and addition interprets addition and multiplication.

In the other direction, PA interprets membership by binary-bit membership.
Bitwise inclusion gives \(x\leq a\), so induction through the finite range
up to \(a\) constructs a cover for each fixed translated formula. This is
formula-specific comprehension, not a uniform truth predicate. Freshening,
substitution, relational term translation, and proof concatenation supply
primitive-recursive finite-proof transformations. Their correctness is
proved by syntactic induction in PA, yielding the asserted PA-provable
consistency equivalence.

arbitrary graph parameters. The theory packet's six diagnostic suites
were also rerun in normal and optimized Python. Those finite diagnostics

\begin{abstract}
The five complete 209-state submissions in the requested ProveIt snapshot
represent two rooted transition-graph isomorphism classes, rather than five
different machine designs. All execute the same 3,909 primitive instructions
and the same 5,083 ordinal control edges. We compare their exact tables,
source arrangements, reconstruction methods, and proof boundaries.

The new construction deletes native state 211 by sharing native state 172.
Two entry invariants, established from complete predecessor histories of
length at most three, distinguish the required behaviors. The resulting
machine has \textbf{208 working states and 416 transitions}, including blank
initialization. Exactly three retained transition rows change, two rows are
deleted, and no source instruction or source address changes.

Four complete local cases prove halting equivalence with the supplied U209
parent on every common initial tape from state 0. Old steps expand to one,
three, or seven new steps. A separate fresh symbolic derivation verifies all
5,084 arbitrary-value primitive contracts and all 416 literal rows. The exact
48,140-step blank initialization is preserved. The same reduction applies
to all five proposals; a second, structurally distinct 208-state variant is
also supplied.

The new local preservation theorem is independent of the logical calibration.
The intended $\Con(\UU)$ and $\Con(\PA)$ endpoint composes it with the
retained conventional proof-search and interpretation arguments. This packet
does not provide a new end-to-end Lean, Rocq, MM0, or exported PA proof
certificate. It also preserves a concrete counterexample to a tempting
source-reassociation shortcut, so that the unsuccessful attempt is not
mistaken for a second valid reduction.
\end{abstract}

\section{Complete preservation proof}\label{sec:proof}
\subsection{Two entry invariants of the old machine}
For a configuration with head at $h$, let $t(j)$ denote the tape bit at
offset $j$, that is, at coordinate $h+j$.
All inventories in this subsection refer to the \emph{old} machine $M$.
The full incoming-edge lists are:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}rl@{}}
\toprule
Target & All incoming transitions\\
\midrule
172 & $116/0\mapsto\act0R{172}$\\
116 & $216/1\mapsto\act1R{116}$\\
211 & $163/0\mapsto\act0L{211}$,\quad
       $163/1\mapsto\act1R{211}$\\
163 & $132/1\mapsto\act1R{163}$,\quad
       $199/1\mapsto\act1R{163}$,\quad
       $214/0\mapsto\act0R{163}$\\
214 & $204/1\mapsto\act1R{214}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
None of these states is the initial state 0. Consequently, every visit on
a run starting at 0 has the necessary predecessor history, regardless
of the initial tape.

Otherwise the last step was $163/0$, which wrote zero and moved left.
The scanned cell at old 211 is then the cell immediately left of the
previous head at 163. An entrance to 163 through $132/1$ or $199/1$ would
have written one in this cell, contradicting the present read-zero condition.
The entrance to 163 must therefore have been $214/0$, a right move after
writing zero. The only entrance to 214 is $204/1$, which wrote one in the
cell now immediately left of the head at 211. The intermediate two steps
do not change that cell. Hence $t(-1)=1$.
\end{proof}

The argument for Lemma~\ref{lem:211} uses at most three predecessor
transitions. The independent checker enumerates all such suffix histories
and all assignments to their touched cells; it does not sample a finite
prefix of the blank run. Unread exterior cells remain arbitrary.

\subsection{Global simulation and its converse}
\begin{theorem}[All-common-tapes preservation]\label{thm:global}
For every binary tape and common initial head position, the runs of $M$ and
$N$ from state 0 halt together. At aligned macro boundaries, their tapes
and heads are equal and their states are related by $\rho$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The initial configurations satisfy the relation because $\rho(0)=0$.
Suppose the relation holds at an old-step boundary. If the old state is
neither 172 nor 211, the corresponding new transition is exactly its
quotient under $\rho$. All 414 such old rows are checked literally.
If the old state is 172 or 211, the relevant guard follows from
Lemmas~\ref{lem:172}--\ref{lem:211}, and one of the four proved macros
restores the relation. Every macro takes a positive number of steps, at most
seven, and none halts internally.

The guards concern old boundary configurations. They need not hold at every
intermediate new configuration, and the argument does not assume that they do.
This distinction is essential because the seven-step case passes through
the representative state at an intermediate head position.

\begin{corollary}[Exact time accounting]\label{cor:time}
For any aligned finite prefix, let $n_{172,0}$ and $n_{211,0}$ count old
steps using the two zero rows. Then
\[
 T_N=T_M+6n_{172,0}+2n_{211,0},
 \qquad T_M\le T_N\le7T_M.
\]
The same identity holds for a halting run.
\end{corollary}
This comparison is directly with the supplied Plain U209 table. Unlike the
earlier source-reassociation constructions, the new reduction changes no
addresses, so no separate source-layout stage lies outside the time bound.
It is a reduction of finite-control size, not a claimed speedup.

The external theorem allows arbitrary binary tapes as functions on the
integers. The internal PA statement quantifies coded finite input data and
finite computation histories, including the blank instance. It does not
introduce second-order quantification over arbitrary tape functions into PA.
The packet supplies the finite certificates and the mathematical induction,
not an exported derivation in a PA proof language.

the $h$-only halt test. It does not affect the axiom selectors because
their selected heads and gates differ from $1$. The original
generalization word is unchanged: it uses PUSH, an offset, one Shift,

Suppose $p$ proves $A$ of code $a$ and $q$ proves $A\to B$ of code
$\mathsf I(a,b)$. Define the new compiler recursively by retaining
the original axiom selectors and generalization clause, and replacing
its MP clause with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:new-mp-word-audit}
 \mathsf{DROP}\;\mathsf{PUSH}\;C(q)\;\mathsf{PUSH}\;
 C(p)\;\mathsf{PUSH}\;\mathsf{SHIFT}^{2}\;
 \mathsf{MP}(b)\;\mathsf{SHIFT}.
\end{equation}
The initial DROP and PUSH insert a zero below both premises. Starting
with $(t,w,0,0)$, unless a recursive call already halts, the states at
the significant boundaries are
\[

 \text{after the first DROP and PUSH}&(0,0::w,0,0)\\

\end{array}

The second Shift halts if $a=1$, and the last Shift halts if $b=1$.
Both conclusions hold for either halt test: at these tests $t=0$.

the failing frame, and a reproducible blank-run check. An exhaustive
784-action attempt to repair one existing routing row found no repair
within that narrowly specified family. No impossibility claim follows.

The searches targeted changes that could be justified by small proofs:
local state folds, head-offset identifications, alternative AX grammars,
source specializations and register layouts. A positive table would still
require the source, startup and consistency bridges. A negative bounded
search establishes only that no candidate passed that search's predicate.

The local checker computes an overapproximation of reachable configurations
in a window $[-k,k]$ around the head. A move introduces either value at
the newly exposed boundary cell. Starting from the blank configuration
makes the abstraction sound for all actual blank-run windows. The
replacement checker then refuses any unmodeled exterior read and requires
exact equality of tape, head and projected state at the endpoint.

Searches included pairs with an identical branch, pairs whose branch
actions have short equivalent continuations, changes to both rows,
single-state bypasses, and head offsets of two cells. The finite-window
constraints were tried at radii four and five in the recorded runs, with
explicit local step limits. No verified one-state saving was found for
the baseline or the result-in-$H$ variant. The more elaborate same-count
helper strategy from the 208 packets was also tested on 8,061,300
two-disjoint-pair/add-one-helper proposals and yielded no survivor in its
35-step local scope.

These results do not exhaust all possible tape invariants. The successful
208 reduction itself illustrates why a previously unexamined conditional
context can matter. In particular, failure of this finite-window procedure
does not prove that two roles cannot be identified by a stronger invariant
or a different simulation relation.

The main AX macro word has length 201 and a 68-node binary DAG.
Rotations and reparsing can alter the number of distinct subtrees and
the availability of predecessor-bit folds. A raw grammar count is not
the full objective: a layout must also preserve the resolved source
control-flow graph, the maximum zero-run constraint of the return scanner,
every arithmetic entry into a shared decoder, and the blank initializer.

One recorded priced search performed 59,686 rotations and priced 46,294
distinct trees in 240 seconds; its best physical count remained 196.
Separate catalog searches retained hundreds of equal-count layouts.
The no-long-zero-run catalog retained 129 layouts priced at 196 among
18,922 priced layouts. Additional local-fold searches on the recorded
catalogs, including 68 compatible layouts with the new MP branch, found
no accepted 195-state table.

A restricted dictionary-segmentation mixed-integer model was also run
for 180 seconds. It recovered a 68-node grammar and left a relaxation
gap. The numerical solver bound applies only to its finite dictionary
model; it is neither a bound on all grammars nor a bound on Turing-machine
state count. It is not used as a theorem in this report.

Deleting one stage from the seven-zero left scanner fails concrete source
frames, including site 0 with path \code{000000} and site 25 with path
\code{100000}. In one site-0 example the original reaches its correct
successor in 486 steps; the shortened scanner instead produces a spurious
root at head offset $+8$ after 236 steps. Bypassing dense state 2 by state
3 also fails the primitive frame contracts.

Dropping the final source continuation is harmless for an abstract cyclic
driver, but it moves the final increment into a right-child leaf position.
The current hardware routes its occurrences as left-child leaves. That
source-level observation therefore does not yet provide a physical state
deletion.

The upstream formal theorem is
\[
 \mathrm{PA}\vdash \neg H_{196}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{PA}).
\]
Its separate Lean proof of standard-model nonhalting does not, by itself,
establish the converse implication in PA. The converse has a direct
syntactic proof. The purpose of this section is to specify that proof and
to isolate it from the external hereditarily finite model used upstream.
The additional compiler described below has not been implemented or checked
in Lean in this package.
\subsection{A syntactic interpretation into PA}

The special code $0$ requires an explicit convention. The arithmetic
operation $\mathrm I(0,0)$ also gives $0$, while the decoder reads $0$ as
truth. These two readings are propositionally equivalent. A proof compiler
uses this fixed equivalence in the zero case; it must not assert literal
syntactic equality between the two readings. Code $1$ translates to
$\beta(x_0,x_0)$, whose negation has a fixed PA proof.

There is a related normalization for derived connectives. Coded negation
$\mathrm N(c)=\mathrm I(c,1)$ initially translates to
$\tau(c)\to\beta(x_0,x_0)$, not to literal arithmetic negation.
The fixed PA theorem $\forall x\,\neg\beta(x,x)$ gives a uniform proof
that these are equivalent. The same normalization applies to coded
conjunction and existential quantification, including inside binders.
These fixed normalization proofs are part of the axiom templates below;
the argument does not silently decode code $1$ as a primitive falsity
symbol.

Take
\[
 \psi(x)= (x=b\lor\beta(a,x))\land\varphi(x)
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad n=a+b+1.
\]
All possible members of $a$, as well as the distinguished point $b$, are
below $n$. Formula~\eqref{eq:finite-comprehension-audit} yields a number $s$
with
\[
 \forall x\;\bigl(\beta(s,x)\leftrightarrow
       ((x=b\lor\beta(a,x))\land\varphi(x))\bigr).
\]
In particular,
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\forall x\;((\beta(a,x)\to\varphi(x)\to\beta(s,x))
       \land(\beta(s,x)\to\varphi(x))),\\
 &\varphi(b)\to\beta(s,b).
 \end{split}
\]
This is the pointed-separation statement needed by the gate.

All six remaining axiom heads translate to fixed logical or equality
theorem schemas. The restricted propositional head translates to a
classical tautology; its numerical restriction does not affect soundness.
The translation respects modus ponens and generalization. Thus there is a
primitive recursive proof compiler $J$ for which PA proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:compiler-sound-audit}
 \operatorname{Der}_{196}(d,c)\longrightarrow
 \operatorname{Prf}_{\mathrm{PA}}(J(d),\tau(c)).
\end{equation}
When $c=1$, compose with the fixed proof of
$\neg\beta(x_0,x_0)$ to obtain a PA refutation. This is the precise
syntactic replacement for an appeal to external semantic soundness.

More explicitly, define $J$ by recursion on the annotated proof tree.
At an axiom leaf insert its fixed logical/equality proof template, or
the comprehension template just constructed for a gate. At an MP node
append the translated premise proofs and one MP step, inserting the
fixed zero-code equivalence when necessary. At a generalization node
append the corresponding generalization. The usual finite-proof list
concatenation and reindexing operations are primitive recursive. An
induction on the coded proof tree verifies the output proof predicate.
This defines the mathematical compiler; writing its concrete Gödel-code
implementation and verifying that implementation in Lean remain separate
tasks.

Project the auxiliary machine traces to the literal 196-state machine by
relabeling their control vectors. The upstream theorem
\path{StateMapTrace.step_maps} proves the pointwise projection for every
nonpadding control. The same finite table check preserves that property
at each next step. All physical root frames have the fixed nonpadding
control $81$, so induction along any positive frame continuation proves
the required projection, with unchanged length and tape vectors. The
packaged theorem \path{StateMapProjection.segment_to_literal} is
specialized to blank-start halting segments; the positive-segment version
just described is an additional composition obligation, not a claim that
this specialized theorem already proves nonhalting. Apply the principle
below to the projected continuations. An independent backwards simulation
is not needed.

Applied to the proof-code invariant, the startup trace and the two levels
of macro simulation, this gives the mathematical implication
\[
 \mathrm{PA}\vdash \operatorname{Con}(\mathrm{PA})\longrightarrow\neg H_{196}.
\]
Together with the upstream arithmetized refutation-to-halting compiler it
gives the desired biconditional. Its exact implementation status must remain
visible: the upstream Lean library checks the latter compiler and external
nonhalting; it does not contain the syntactic interpretation compiler $J$
or the foregoing PA-internal proof-code safety theorem. A Lean certification
of the full biconditional requires adding those modules and the positive
segment and invariant compositions just described. No such certification
is supplied here.

The native scalar calculi in ConciseIPRA are proved equivalent to iPRA,
whose induction is quantifier-free. They do not by that fact furnish a
refutation calculus for full PA. In particular the uniform finite
comprehension proof above uses the full induction instance containing
the arbitrary translated formula $\varphi$. Replacing the present calculus
by an iPRA calculus without supplying the missing strength would change the
consistency problem. Useful transferable ideas are operational: deriving
equality rules from other rules, choosing antecedent order for shared
instruction trees, and using a literal syntactic feature to select a rule
mode. Those ideas are applicable only after the full-PA proof translations
are re-established.

# Formal theorem statements

The literal machine is `PA196.Literal.machine`. It starts in state 0 with an

The paper states the roles of PA consistency and standard-model soundness
explicitly. The closed Lean corollaries use Foundation's standard-model

\begin{abstract}
We give a two-symbol Turing machine with 196 working states that
searches for a contradiction in ordinary first-order Peano arithmetic.
It runs forever on a blank tape. Peano arithmetic proves neither its
exact arithmetic halting sentence nor its negation. The machine's
axiom command reverses the two arguments in the quantifier code and
uses a guarded equality-vacuity clause in place of a primitive
transitivity head. In Lean~4 we verify the calculus, the simulation
of the register program, and both unprovability results for the
literal table.
\end{abstract}

Let $M$ be the machine in Section~\ref{sec:machine}, and let $M_{209}$
be its predecessor~\cite{pa209}. Write $\PA$ for ordinary first-order
Peano arithmetic. The arithmetic halting sentence $H$ uses the rows
of $M$ in the trace formula of~\cite[\S5]{pa209}.

The tape has alphabet $\{0,1\}$ and is infinite in both directions.
It starts with all cells zero. State $0$ is the start state,
$0,\ldots,195$ are the working states, and $196$ is the halt label. In state $q$, a row
$(q,b,w,D,q')$ reads $b$, writes $w$, moves one cell in direction $D$,
and enters $q'$. The table has one row for each pair in
$\{0,\ldots,195\}\times\{0,1\}$. The file \file{data/pa196.tm} contains
all 392 rows and has SHA-256 digest
\begin{quote}\small
\nolinkurl{e8bbccd4cfa325251ca95066db116b5aa766e404b0971c33c02772be1c3617a8}.
\end{quote}
The first row is $(0,0,1,R,1)$, and $(63,1,1,R,196)$ is the only row
that enters the halt label.

As in $M_{209}$, a tape engine interprets a register program stored
as a binary tree. A \emph{frame} records a marker, the path to the
current site, a gap, and the register file. A block $0\,1^{v+1}$
stores value $v$~\cite[\S3]{pa209}. The engine's 36 states have
the same rows as in $M_{209}$ after renaming. Of the remaining states,
13 route leaf instructions to the engine and 147 read the 159
distinct nodes. State $75$ reads the root.

The register program of $M_{209}$ enumerates words over three commands
on a store $(t,w,d,h)$. It halts when Shift reads formula code
$1$~\cite[\S4]{pa209}. We keep Shift and $\mpc$, change $\ax(c,x,y)$
in three steps, and then change how the program stores that command.

Let $p(a,b)=\binom{a+b+1}{2}+b$. The four constructors in $M_{209}$
use $4p(a,b)+r$, where $r=0,1,2,3$ denotes implication, membership,
universal quantification and equality, respectively. The constructors
in $M$ are
\[
 \Ic(a,b)=4p(a,b),\quad \Mc(a,b)=4p(a,b)+1,\quad
 \Uc(a,B)=4p(B,a)+2,\quad \Ec(a,b)=4p(a,b)+3 .
\]
Only the quantifier code reverses the pairing arguments. As before,
code $0$ is truth and $1=\Mc(0,0)$ is the contradiction. Write
$\Nc(B)=\Ic(B,1)$, $B\wedge C=\Nc(\Ic(B,\Nc(C)))$,
$B\leftrightarrow C$ for $\Ic(B,C)\wedge\Ic(C,B)$, and
$\exists x_a\,B$ for $\Nc(\Uc(a,\Nc(B)))$. An arrow in the formulas
below denotes $\Ic$.

In $M_{209}$, $\ax$ pushes the saved top, a generalization, the
restricted propositional head $\rho_8$ and seven further heads
$\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_7$. It leaves a guarded gate in $t$.
For $\ax(c,x,y)$ in $M$, put $D=d+x$, $H=h+y$ and $A=c$. The command
pushes the saved top $t$, the generalization $\Uc(d,h)$, the head
\[
 \rho_8(D,A,H,d)=\bigl((H\to d)\to D\bigr)\to\bigl((D\to H)\to(A\to H)\bigr),
\]
and then the six formulas of Table~\ref{tab:heads}, in that order.

The body of $\ax$ is a straight-line sequence of 201 items. Its macro
calls come from~\cite{pa209}. They push the accumulator, push it and
load one of the three registers, pop and form $4p$, read the two
parameters, or check the two parts of the guard. The other items are
single increments of the accumulator and the closing jump. The full
program has $3{,}812$ sites, compared with $3{,}948$ for $M_{209}$.

\begin{lemma}[Program]\label{lem:program}
Outside the body of $\ax$ the register program $R$ of $M$ agrees with
that of $M_{209}$ after translation of addresses. The body of $\ax$ is a concatenation of blocks, each
identical to a macro block of $M_{209}$ and left only to the next
block. It computes the saved top, $\Uc(d,h)$, $\rho_8(D,A,H,d)$, the
six formulas of Table~\ref{tab:heads} and the gate $F(H,D,A)$, in the
codes of Step~1.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
After flattening the program and translating the addresses, the 169
sites outside the body agree with $M_{209}$. The 201 blocks use the
same macros and internal jump offsets. The closing jump goes to the
corresponding successor. The macro contracts give the store effect of
each block. Symbolic execution gives the nine stack entries and the
new top as formula trees over $4p(\cdot,\cdot)+r$, with the argument
order of Step~1. Lean checks the source program in
\file{PA196/Program.lean} and the effect of the command in
\file{PA196/Source/AXEffect.lean}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Use the interpretation of membership and equality
from~\cite[\S4.2]{pa209}. In a model of $\PA$, $\Mc(a,b)$ says that
bit $x_b$ of $x_a$ is set. Each formula in Table~\ref{tab:heads} is
either a head of~\cite{pa209}, possibly with two antecedents exchanged,
or the witness formula $\exists x_a(x_b=x_a)$. Each is true under every
assignment, as is the propositional tautology $\rho_8$.

A formula is \emph{derivable} if modus ponens and generalization give
a proof from instances of the six heads, $\rho_8$ with $u\le a$, and
the gate with $c\ne a,b$. The proofs below use fixed finite templates
in the labels and codes. Their case distinctions compare numbers
for equality. PA can carry out these arguments on coded proofs by the
method of~\cite[\S6.1]{pa209}.

In the Lean development of~\cite{pa209}, only
\file{ActualCertificateNeighborhoodPrimitive.lean} uses $\rho_7$
directly. It derives reflexivity and symmetry of primitive equality
and vacuity of $\Ec(a,b)$ under the label $\Mc(a,b)$.
\file{ActualCertificateNeighborhoodCongruence.lean} uses symmetry
to reverse the membership rewrites $\rho_3,\rho_5$.
\file{ActualCertificateNeighborhoodWitness.lean} uses symmetry and
vacuity to prove $\Ec(a,b)\to\Rc(a,b,z)$ for $z\ne a,b$, where
\[
 \Rc(a,b,z)=\Uc\bigl(z,\Mc(a,z)\leftrightarrow\Mc(b,z)\bigr)\wedge
            \Uc\bigl(z,\Mc(z,a)\leftrightarrow\Mc(z,b)\bigr)
\]
is the equality relation of the interpretation. The same module
then gets $\exists x_a\,\Rc(a,c,z)$ from $\rho_1$. The rest of the
proof uses primitive equality through the following three facts.
\begin{description}
\item[(R)] For all labels $a,b,d$, both
  $\Ec(a,b)\to(\Mc(d,a)\leftrightarrow\Mc(d,b))$ and
  $\Ec(a,b)\to(\Mc(a,d)\leftrightarrow\Mc(b,d))$.
\item[(N)] $\Ec(a,b)\to\Rc(a,b,z)$ for $z\ne a,b$.
\item[(W)] An existential witness for equality at every pair of labels.
\end{description}
We derive (R), (N) and (W) directly. They suffice for the interpretation
in place of separate laws for symmetry and transitivity of primitive
equality.

For $d\ne a$, \eqref{eq:chi} with $\chi(t)=\Mc(d,t)$ and with
$\chi(t)=\Mc(t,d)$ are the two statements. For $d=a$ the statements
are $\Ec(a,b)\to(\Mc(a,b)\to\Mc(a,a))$ and
$\Ec(a,b)\to(\Mc(b,a)\to\Mc(a,a))$. Head~3 gives
$\Ec(a,b)\to(\Mc(a,b)\to\Mc(b,b))$, head~4 gives
$\Ec(a,b)\to(\Mc(b,a)\to\Mc(b,b))$, and~\eqref{eq:chi} with
$\chi(t)=\Mc(t,t)$ gives $\Ec(a,b)\to(\Mc(b,b)\to\Mc(a,a))$.
\end{proof}

In the interpretation, separation gives a set $x_c$ that contains
$x_a$ if $x_a$ lacks $\chi$ and contains only elements that lack
$\chi$. Since $x_b$ belongs to every set that contains $x_a$, if
$x_b$ has $\chi$, then $x_a$ has it too. The calculus specializes a
quantifier with a witness from head~5 and direct rewrites. These
steps supply the specialization without a substitution rule.

At a node, the state reads the path bit, moves right and enters the
state for the corresponding child. Leaves are instructions, and
the machine stores equal subtrees once. The 201 items in the body of
$\ax$ form the leaves of a binary tree with 68 distinct internal
nodes.

As in $M_{209}$, two nodes can share a state if one occurs only as a
left child and the other only as a right child. When the current bit
would select different children for the two nodes, the shared state
moves left to the bit that selected the node. A second state reads
that bit again and moves right into a third state, which uses the
current bit to choose the correct child. Both states already read
other nodes or start a macro, so sharing requires no extra states.

nodes.

We remove two states outside the body that $M_{209}$ used to
distinguish nodes of its old body. Each read a single symbol and

now performs the successor's action directly.

\begin{lemma}[One instruction]\label{lem:contract}
For every site of $R$ and each outcome of a conditional decrement,
the machine $M$ started in state $75$ on a valid clean frame of
that site with gap at least 48 reaches, in at least one step, the clean frame of the
successor site with the register effect of the instruction. At the
halt site it enters the halt label.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A run from a clean frame alternates between walks outside the engine
and calls to the engine. The engine rows match those of $M_{209}$.
The register lemmas of~\cite[\S3]{pa209} apply for the same register
contents and gaps. They cover filling the gap, marking a register,
incrementing, both outcomes of decrementing, updating the path and
scanning back. The return scan ends on the cell after the first $1$
with seven zeros to its left. For most sites that cell is the root.
At 19 sites one pass ends on a later path cell, where the next walk
begins, as in $M_{209}$.

In the computed runs, states outside the engine read only path
cells and the two cells after the path. These reads stay at or to the
right of the root. At each site and for each outcome, the walk visits
the same sequence of states, cells and symbols for every register
file tested. One run thus determines the fixed sequence of rows
and engine calls for the contract.

[Paper (PDF)](paper/pa209.pdf) · [Transition table](data/pa209.tm) ·
[Formal statements](docs/result.md) · [Reproduction](docs/reproduction.md)

# Formal theorem statements

The literal machine is `M6.Literal.machine`. Its initial configuration is
`M6.Startup.blank`, state 0 on a blank binary tape. Ordinary Peano arithmetic
is Foundation's first-order theory `Peano`, with full induction.
Let `H` denote `ExactHaltingFormula.traceSentence` and `N` its negation.

| Lean declaration | Statement |
| --- | --- |
| `M6.Arithmetic.PA.FinalEndpoint.literal_final_endpoint` | Under PA consistency, the exact machine has 209 working states and 418 rows, runs forever, and its exact arithmetic nonhalting sentence is true and unprovable in PA. |
| `M6.PA.literal_nonhalting` | Under PA consistency, the literal machine never halts from the blank tape. |
| `M6.Arithmetic.PA.FinalEndpoint.nonhalting_true` | Under PA consistency, the natural numbers satisfy `N`. |
| `M6.Arithmetic.PA.FinalEndpoint.pa_proves_nonhalting_consistency` | PA proves `N → Con(PA)`. |
| `M6.Arithmetic.PA.FinalEndpoint.nonhalting_unprovable` | Under PA consistency, PA cannot prove `N`. |
| `M6.Arithmetic.PA.ExactHaltingFormula.literal_binding` | Each active arithmetic row agrees with the corresponding physical transition after state relabeling. |
| `M6.Arithmetic.PA.Independence.nonhalting_irrefutable` | Under PA consistency, standard-model soundness excludes a PA proof of `¬N`. |
| `M6.Arithmetic.PA.Independence.halting_unprovable` | PA cannot prove the positive halting sentence `H`. |
| `M6.Arithmetic.PA.Independence.two_sided_independence` | PA can prove neither `N` nor `¬N`. |
| `M6.Arithmetic.PA.Independence.machine_nonhalting` | The literal machine never halts from the blank tape. |

[Challenge](../Challenge.lean) states both headline results with explicit

\begin{abstract}
We give an explicit two-symbol Turing machine with 209 working states
that searches for a contradiction in ordinary first-order Peano
arithmetic. The machine runs forever on a blank tape, and Peano
arithmetic proves neither its exact arithmetic halting sentence nor
its negation. The construction connects a register-program simulation
to a refutation compiler that works in every model of Peano arithmetic.
The literal transition table, both unprovability directions, and
blank-tape nonhalting are formalized in Lean~4.
\end{abstract}

Busy Beaver problems ask how long a halting machine of a fixed size can
run~\cite{rado}. Explicit small machines whose behavior is independent of
a specified theory also give concrete examples of incompleteness.
Yedidia and Aaronson constructed such a machine for ZFC~\cite{yedidia}.
Here the theory is ordinary first-order Peano arithmetic with full
induction, denoted by $\PA$. This construction reduces the working-state
count from the earlier 211-state construction for $\PA$~\cite{pa211}.
The register engine draws on the K230 construction~\cite{k230}, and
its proof calculus uses ingredients from the PA238 development~\cite{pa238}
and Reshetnikov's restricted implication proof~\cite{proveit}.

Write $M$ for the machine in Section~\ref{sec:machine}. Let $H$ be the
sentence of arithmetic defined in Section~\ref{sec:arith}, and put
$N=\neg H$. Write $\PA\vdash A$ for the existence of a finite formal
derivation of $A$ from $\PA$. The statement $\Con(\PA)$, used inside
arithmetic, is the syntactic consistency sentence for the standard
provability predicate.

Under the external assumption of $\PA$ consistency, the machine runs
forever and $\PA\nvdash N$. The proof of $\PA\nvdash H$ uses the
soundness of $\PA$ in the standard natural numbers. In ordinary classical
mathematics that standard model also establishes consistency. Lean
uses the standard-model theorems for Foundation's theory
\texttt{Peano}~\cite{foundation}. The published statement has an explicit
presentation of the ordinary $\PA$ proof calculus, with its equivalence
to Foundation's presentation proved in the Solution.

The tape is infinite in both directions, with alphabet $\{0,1\}$ and
initially all cells zero. State $0$ is the initial state. The working
state labels are
\[
            Q=\{0,\ldots,213\}\setminus\{50,122,150,157,205\}.
\]
A row $(q,b,w,D,q')$ reads $b$ at state $q$, writes $w$, moves one cell in
direction $D$, and enters $q'$. There is one row for every pair
in $Q\times\{0,1\}$. The state $215$ terminates the run. The 418 rows are
given in \src{data/pa209.tm}{data/pa209.tm}, with SHA-256 digest
\begin{quote}\small
\nolinkurl{0610d978675320f0b4b1ef34619dcd3daa5912632d7037e200dfcc70954fea51}.
\end{quote}
For example, the first row is $(0,0,1,R,1)$ and the transition
$(68,1,1,R,215)$ enters the halt state. Lean checks closure of all row
targets in $Q\cup\{215\}$ and the count of distinct working states.

The exact startup takes $58{,}210$ tape steps. It reaches the frame for
source site $25$ at literal control $81$, with the candidate register
equal to $2$ and every other logical register zero. The complete
register file, in its physical order, is
\[
              (0,0,0,0,0,0,2,0,0,1^{[26]}),
\]
where $1^{[26]}$ denotes 26 further entries equal to $1$. The prefix
checks the full tape and head, including those spare entries. The
definitions and proof are in \src{M6/Startup/Data.lean}{M6/Startup/Data.lean}
and \src{M6/Startup.lean}{M6/Startup.lean}.

A frame contains the source path, header and marker, and a register
file in which a value $v$ is represented by a block $0\,1^{v+1}$.
The physical proof relabels the literal controls, sending the start
and halt to $74$ and $254$ respectively. The relabeling commutes with
each step, preserving the two tape lists. The resulting contracts
are proved for every source site and for both outcomes of a conditional
decrement. Each contract takes a frame to the complete frame of its
source successor in a positive number of tape steps, or implements the
source halt. The proof combines the finite control diagrams with the
unary arithmetic and register-file lemmas. It checks source addresses,
control destinations, and register effects separately.

Let $p(a,b)=\binom{a+b+1}{2}+b$ be Cantor pairing. Formula codes use
$I(a,b)=4p(a,b)$ for implication and $U(a,b)=4p(a,b)+2$ for
universal quantification. The two atomic forms have residues $1$ and
$3$ for membership and equality. Code $0$ is truth, and code $1$
decodes as $x_0\in x_0$. The decoder interprets implication into
code $1$ as negation. The calculus uses modus ponens and
generalization, and its axiom formulas are the exact constructors in
\src{M6/Source/ActualAXCode.lean}{ActualAXCode.lean}. The eighth head
requires a dominance condition on its fourth parameter. The
separation formula at the gate has the two indicated freshness
conditions on the third variable.

A store $(t,w,d,h)$ has two visible formula codes $t,h$, a stack $w$
encoded by iterated pairing, and a variable-label offset $d$.
Write $p_L,p_R$ for the total Cantor projections. The three
commands are as follows.
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lp{0.74\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
Command & Effect \\
\midrule
$\shift$ & Halt if $t+h=1$. Otherwise replace $(t,w,h)$ by
$(h,p_R(w),p_L(w))$. \\
$\mpc(x)$ & Put $y=d+x$. If $h=I(t,y)$, return $(y,p(0,w),y,0)$.
Otherwise return $(0,w,y,0)$. \\
$\ax(c,x,y)$ & Put $a=d+x$ and $b=h+y$. Push eight axiom heads,
$U(d,h)$, and the saved top $t$. Set $t$ to the guarded separation
formula, or to truth when $c=a$ or $c=b$. Set $d=h=0$. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The sixth head in this ordering is
\[
   \rho_6(a,b)=I\bigl(\ulcorner\exists x_a\,\forall x_a\,B\urcorner,b\bigr),
\]
where $B$ has code $b$ and the quantifiers use the numeric constructors.
The choice of arguments follows from the checked copy operations in
Section~\ref{sec:physical}. The other seven heads and the
generalization head keep their stated parameter dependence.

Interpret $y\in x$ in a model of $\PA$ as the statement that bit $y$ of
$x$ is set. The uniform axiom suppliers establish truth under this
interpretation, including pointed separation and the guarded
implicational schema. Modus ponens and generalization preserve
validity. The relation $y\in x$ implies $y<x$, so code $1$ is false
under every assignment in this interpretation. Soundness for an
actual finite derivation, followed by first-order completeness, gives
a $\PA$ refutation if code $1$ has a proof in the command calculus.

Encode a tape by natural numbers $l,r$. Their low bits are respectively
the cell just to the left of the head and the scanned cell. Higher bits
run away from the head. Missing high bits represent zero. For a
right-moving row $(q_0,b,w,R,q_1)$ use the arithmetic relation
\[
  q=q_0\land q'=q_1\land
  \exists u\,(r=2u+b\land l'=2l+w\land r'=u).
\]
For a left-moving row use
\begin{align*}
 q=q_0\land q'=q_1\land\exists u,v,e\,(&
    (e=0\lor e=1)\land l=2v+e\land r=2u+b\\
    &{}\land l'=v\land r'=2(2u+w)+e).
\end{align*}
Let $F(q,l,r,q',l',r')$ be the disjunction of these formulas over
the 418 rows. These formulas use the published state labels. Writing
sequence access in subscript notation, the halting sentence is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:halt}
 H:=\exists n,Q_*,L_*,R_*\,
 \left[
 \begin{aligned}
 &Q_0=L_0=R_0=0\land Q_n=215\\[-2pt]
 &{}\land\forall i<n\ F(Q_i,L_i,R_i,Q_{i+1},L_{i+1},R_{i+1})
 \end{aligned}
 \right].
\end{equation}
The three sequence variables range over arithmetic codes. Each access
in~\eqref{eq:halt} abbreviates the explicit arithmetic sequence
relation \texttt{nthDef}. In the standard model these relations
describe exactly the finite tape runs. In every model of $\PA$, the
exact formula is equivalent to the auxiliary formula used to compose
coded trace segments. For this equivalence, induction on the coded
step index excludes the six padding labels
$50,122,150,157,205,214$ from a trace starting at zero.
\src{M6PA/Model/ExactHaltingFormula.lean}{ExactHaltingFormula.lean}
proves the row correspondence and the two trace implications.

The arithmetized transport starts with a proof code for $\bot$ in
ordinary $\PA$. It translates the sequent proof to the presentation
with successor, and then interprets that presentation in the numeric
calculus of membership and equality. The interpretation uses the
finite ordinal domain with zero and ordinal successor, and treats
equality by the ordinal isomorphism relation. The axiom suppliers
realize the arithmetic defining equations and the induction scheme
by separation and ordinal induction. Logical inference is
transported by arithmetic operations on proof codes. This produces
an accepted certificate for code $1$ uniformly in $V$. The formal
transport is
\src{M6PA/Calibration/FoundationNativeRefutationTransport.lean}{FoundationNativeRefutationTransport.lean}.
It supplies the internal implication from standard $\PA$ provability
of $\bot$ to the existence of a certificate satisfying the exact
refutation-checker graph.

A certificate is $p(f,i)$, with fuel $f$ and a tree code $i$.
A tree code pairs a rule tag with its payload. Payload tuples are
iterated Cantor pairs ending in zero. Tags $0,1$ are modus ponens and
generalization. Tags $2$ through $9$ are the eight axiom heads,
in order, and tag $10$ is the guarded separation instance.
Failed guards, malformed tuples and rejected premises reject the
certificate. The checker returns $a+1$ on accepting formula code
$a$, and returns zero on rejection. Thus the refutation-checker
graph tests output $2$.

For a formal induction in $V$, let $A(f,B)$ be the coded vector of
checker outputs for indices $0,\ldots,B$ at fuel $f$, and let
$W(f,B)$ be the vector of compiled words at the same indices.
The fuel-zero vectors contain rejections and empty words respectively.
A successor row reads the children from the previous vectors,
applies the rule just described, and appends one coded word as one
entry. Let $\mathcal R(w,a)$ mean that, for all $t,z$, running $w$
on $(t,z,0,0)$ halts or returns $(a,z,0,0)$. Full $\PA$ induction on
$f$ proves
\[
 \forall B,i,a\quad A(f,B)_i=a+1
                    \ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal R(W(f,B)_i,a).
\]
At zero fuel the antecedent is false. At successor fuel an accepted
leaf uses its exact selector, a generalization uses the child
hypothesis followed by its suffix, and an MP uses both child
hypotheses followed by the MP suffix. Rejected rows cannot meet the
antecedent. This induction concerns an arithmetic predicate on coded
vectors and stores. It applies to all fuel values in $V$.

The source-to-tape correspondence replaces every step in the coded
source trace by a positive-length coded tape block. It starts from
the full clean frame, concatenates these blocks, and prepends the
certified blank startup. The resulting coded trace ends at state
$215$. The row and trace correspondence in Section~\ref{sec:arith}
puts it in the exact formula $H$. Because $V$ was arbitrary,
first-order completeness gives the internal implication
\[
          \PA\vdash \Prov_{\PA}(\ulcorner\bot\urcorner)\to H,
          \qquad
          \PA\vdash N\to\Con(\PA).
\]
The compiled word, scheduler, and trace construction are checked
separately. The trace endpoint is
\src{M6PA/RefutationHalting.lean}{RefutationHalting.lean} and the final
consistency implication is in \src{M6PA/FinalEndpoint.lean}{FinalEndpoint.lean}.

The Lean endpoint is
\src{M6PA/TwoSidedIndependence.lean}{TwoSidedIndependence.lean}.
\src{Solution.lean}{Solution.lean} transfers the exact formula and
provability predicate to the statements in
\src{Challenge.lean}{Challenge.lean}. The same Solution identifies
its tape semantics with the literal machine and transfers the
blank-tape nonhalting proof. The two statements concern the
particular machine defined by the table in Section~\ref{sec:machine}.

In the relevant 209-state native layout, entry to state 172 has predecessor cells `10`; entry to state 211 while scanning zero has predecessor bit one. Their context-sensitive fold uses a shared helper to distinguish those histories. Its ordinary realization, however, has induction only for literal
equations, derives quantifier-free induction, and is bi-interpretable with

induction. That result does not supply a refutation calculus for full PA.

This project collects the research packages that look for a very small
complete presentation of a theory bi-interpretable with full first-order
intuitionistic primitive recursive arithmetic (iPRA), and the Lean
formalization of the most concise of them.

- [`docs/Article/`](docs/Article/) is the unified article

  written mathematics of all delivered packages merged into eleven chapters,

- [`Artifacts/`](Artifacts/) holds the executable part of the delivered

Every package measures a *complete standalone proof checker*: one Python
module that reads a JSON certificate and accepts exactly the theorems of the
presented calculus. The size coordinates are significant tokens, AST nodes and
UTF-8 bytes of the source after `ast.unparse` normalization (CPython 3.12.14);
gzip sizes are reported for information only. A presentation qualifies only if
its ordinary realization is bi-interpretable with iPRA with both numerical
domains whole, equality actual, and both composites the identity graph `x = y`.

together with the two computation equations. No other logical, successor,
equality or induction axiom is primitive: reflexivity comes from
`I(0, t; u.0) = t`, implication, conjunction, disjunction and the two
quantifiers are macros over `D` built from the selector
`C(v, a, b) := I(v, a; u.b)`, and numerical case distinction and induction for
equations are derived rules.

**Two rules can be weakened.** The Lean kernel (see
[Lean formalization](#lean-formalization)) takes weaker forms of Tr and of DI
by progress as primitive, and proves that the derivable sequents are the same
(`iprf_iff_nprf`):

- *No literal-zero source, for free.* The source `s` of a transport may be
  restricted to terms other than the literal `0`, and for the one-term rule
  this costs nothing (`oprf_iff_nprf`): a constant template reverses any
  equation in one step, because the major premise can be
  `I(0, 0; u.0) = 0`; a term provably zero is joined to the anchor
  `I(0, 0; u.0)` by one transport of `I(0, p; u.0) = p`; and transport along
  `0 = t` is transport along `t = 0` followed by transitivity. No induction,
  numerical case distinction or successor computation is used; the argument
  needs the first computation equation and the rule itself (class `OKernel`).
  This is the theorem of
  [`one_sided_transport`](Artifacts/one_sided_transport/), and it lets the
  source of an elimination select its major premise
  ([`source_dispatch`](Artifacts/source_dispatch/)).

- *All together.* One-term transport at sources other than the literal `0`,
  with the single introduction, is a calculus of seven rules, `MPrf`: Hyp,
  the two computation equations, Tr, QE, DE and DI. It derives the same
  sequents as the calculus of the reports (`mprf_iff_iprf`), and full
  transport is recovered in it without induction.
- *Six rules, closed under substitution.* Eval and the diagonal introduction
  combine: hypothesis, reflexivity, Eval, QE, DE and the introduction whose
  mode is read off the diagonal shape. This calculus, `SPrf`, has no
  computation axiom, no template, no normalization and no test on a witness or
  on a transport source; it derives the same sequents as the kernel
  (`sprf_iff_nprf`) and is closed under substitution by a direct induction on
  derivations (`SPrf.subst`). None of the packages states this combination.
- *Five rules, with clauses in place of `Q`.* The formulas are equations and
  `D` only. A context is a list of clauses `[A; y.B(y)]`, read
  `A → ∀y B(y)`, an ordinary assumption `A` being `[0 = 0; v.A]`. The rules are
  Refl, Eval, Use (from `A` infer `B(t)` for a clause of the context), Elim
  (open `D_{x,y} B` at a fresh `b`, which adds the clause
  `[B(b,0); y.B(b,y)]`) and Intro. This calculus, `CPrf`, derives only
  `Q`-free formulas from `Q`-free clauses (`CPrf.qfree`), agrees with the
  kernel on `Q`-free sequents (`cprf_iff_nprf_of_qfree`), and derives the
  `Q`-free form of every native sequent, with `Q_y B` rewritten as `D_{x,y} B`
  with `x` unused (`cprf_iff_nprf`). This is the raw clause calculus of
  [`raw_clausal`](Artifacts/raw_clausal/) and its successors.
- *One body per context entry.* A clause needs no antecedent field. In
  `OBPrf` a context entry is one body `B(y)`, read `B(0) → ∀y B(y)`, which is
  the kernel formula `Q_y B`; Use infers `B(t)` from `B(0)`, Open adds the
  body `B(b, y)`, and the assumption of Intro is stored as the gate body
  `gate_v A`, the formula `A` with `sel(v, 0, ·)` on both sides of its
  equation. `obprf_iff_nprf : OBPrf (Γ.map gb) A ↔ NPrf Γ A` on `Q`-free
  sequents, `obprf_unQ_iff_nprf` in general, and `obprf_iff_cprf` against
  `CPrf` (`NativeOneBody`). An opened clause of `CPrf` is already one body,
  so the translation is literal except where an assumption is used. There
  the gate body gives `gate_1 A` by Use, and `A` follows by conversion along
  `sel(1, 0, s) = s` under the binders of `A`; conversion at a binder needs
  access one level down, so the two are proved together by induction on the
  number of binders (`OBPrf.conv`, `OBPrf.access`). No cut or weakening of
  `OBPrf` is used. This is the calculus of
  [`one_body`](Artifacts/one_body/).

  `v0prf_iff_nprf`).
- *Equality at the discharge of a witness.* On full normal forms one rule,
  Name, replaces both transport and DE: from `D_{x,y} B`, and from `b = t` and
  `F` in the context opened at a fresh `b`, infer `F[t/b]`, provided it does
  not mention `b`. With `t = b` it is DE. The kernel then has six rules, Hyp,
  Refl, Name, QE, DI by cases and QI by progress (`NMPrf`, `nmprf_iff_nprf`).
  The naming packet gives `b = t` and `h(b) = u` in the opened context, and
  Name exports `h(t) = u`: transport without the crossing
  (`NMPrf.packet`). At the template `x` with a reflexive equation that is
  symmetry, and the transport of the kernel follows. This is the rule of
  [`witness_discharge`](Artifacts/witness_discharge/).
- *Five rules.* On full normal forms the two reductions above combine: Name
  in place of transport and DE, and one introduction in place of DI by cases
  and QI by progress. The calculus is Hyp, Refl, Name, QE and that
  introduction (`N5Prf`, `n5prf_iff_nprf`, `n5prf_iff_pra`), with lists of
  formulas as contexts and `Q` in the language: no computation rule, no
  transport, and no separate elimination of `D`. Among the calculi proved
  here whose contexts are formulas it has the fewest rules; the clause
  calculi also have five (`CPrf`, `ZCPrf`) or four families (`VPrf`, `ZVPrf`),
  with clauses in their contexts. This combination is not taken from a
  package.
- *Three rule families.* With clauses in the contexts the five rules become
  three families. `WDPrf` has formulas built from equations and `D` over full
  normal forms, clauses with at most one antecedent, the fixed reflexivity
  clause `[; y. y = y]`, and the rules Use, Intro and Name; Name opens
  `D_{x,y} B` by adding the clause `[B(b, 0); y.B(b, y)]`. There is no `Q`, no
  computation rule, no transport, no reflexivity rule and no separate
  elimination of `D`. `wdprf_iff_nprf` proves that the kernel derives a
  sequent exactly when `WDPrf` derives the full normal form of its `Q`-free
  form from the reflexivity clause and the corresponding assumptions, and
  `wdprf_iff_nprf_of_qfree` is the same statement on `Q`-free sequents. This
  is [`witness_discharge`](Artifacts/witness_discharge/) in its own form, and
  the calculus with the fewest rule families proved here.
- *Three rule families with an inferred witness.* `OCPrf` has the same
  formulas, clauses and reflexivity clause, and the rules Use, Intro and Open.
  Open has one premise fewer than Name and no parameter: from `D_{x,y} B` and
  a derivation of `A` under the clause `[B(r, 0); y.B(r, y)]` it infers `A`,
  where `r` is read off the rows of `B` at a fresh `b` (`b = r` if `B(b, 0)`
  is literally `0 = 0` and `B(b, 1)` is literally `b = r`, and `b` itself
  otherwise). `ocprf_iff_nprf` proves the same equivalence with the kernel
  as for `WDPrf`. Transport is recovered from a packet with the rows `0 = 0`,
  `x = T`, `H(x) = U`, on which Open selects `T`; ordinary elimination of `D`
  is not a derived rule, so kernel derivations are translated under an
  arbitrary substitution. This is
  [`inferred_witness`](Artifacts/inferred_witness/) and
  [`deterministic_opening`](Artifacts/deterministic_opening/) in their own
  form.
- *Three rule families with a deterministic discharge.* `XCPrf` has Use, Intro
  and Discharge: from `D_{x,y} B` and one derivation of `F` under the clause
  `[B(b, 0); y.B(b, y)]` it infers `F[r/b]`, with the same `r` read off the
  rows of `B`. The clause is opened at the fresh variable and the selected
  witness is substituted in the exported formula. Here the ordinary
  elimination of `D` is a derived rule, since the substitution does nothing
  to a formula that does not mention `b`; so `xcprf_iff_nprf` is proved by a
  rule-by-rule translation of the six-rule calculus `F6Prf`, and soundness by
  reading Discharge as Name at the selected witness. This is
  [`first_instance`](Artifacts/first_instance/) and
  [`clause_discharge`](Artifacts/clause_discharge/) in their own form.
- *Five rules with substitution for the newest variable.* `VCPrf` is the
  forward clause calculus of
  [`variable_substitution`](Artifacts/variable_substitution/): Refl, Sub, Use,
  Elim and Intro on full normal forms, with clauses `[A; y.B(y)]` in the
  context and no `Q`. Sub infers `v = u[t/x]` from `x = t` and `u = v` for the
  newest variable `x` only. That rule is not stable under weakening by a new
  variable, so derivations of `VCPrf` cannot be weakened or renamed;
  `vcprf_iff_nprf` is proved by translating the six-rule calculus `F6Prf`
  under an arbitrary renaming of the source, with a context invariant that is
  a membership and not a derivability (`Cl.Inv`, `F6Prf.toVC`).
- *Seven uniform rules, with another reading of `Q`.* `RPrf` is the calculus
  of [`uniform_progress`](Artifacts/uniform_progress/): hypothesis, the two
  computations, transport in an equation template, and QE, DE, DI whose mode
  is read off the root of the matrix alone. No rule looks at a witness, so
  substitution in derivations is a direct induction. The price is the meaning
  of `Q`: at a literal equation it is progressivity, `∀y (E(y) → E(S y))`.
  So `RPrf` is not the kernel on the same formulas; it is equivalent to it
  through a translation. `NFm.emb` pads every equation below a binder to a
  compound formula, and `rprf_emb_iff` proves that the kernel derives a
  sequent exactly when `RPrf` derives its translation. Equation induction
  and transport in arbitrary formulas are derived inside `RPrf`
  (`RPrf.eqInd`, `RPrf.leibniz`). The reading is faithful as well:
  `rprf_iff_rd` proves that `RPrf` derives a sequent exactly when the kernel
  derives its progressive reading, and every formula of `RPrf` is
  interderivable in `RPrf` with the translation of its reading
  (`REquivIn.emb_rd`). With `NEquiv.rd_emb` these are the two formula round
  trips, on all formulas and over arbitrary contexts.
- *The target-directed elimination.* `TQPrf` is `RPrf` with another
  elimination of `Q`, the rule of
  [`target_closure`](Artifacts/target_closure/): from `Q_y B` and `B(δ_B(t))`
  infer `B(t)`, where `δ_B(t)` is `r` when `B` is a literal equation and `t`
  is literally `S r`, and `0` otherwise. One target term is supplied and no
  orbit term. `tqprf_iff_rprf : TQPrf Γ A ↔ RPrf Γ A` proves that the two
  calculi derive the same sequents on the same formulas, so
  `tqprf_emb_iff` gives the equivalence with the kernel. `TQPrf` is stable
  under renaming and not under substitution.
- *One introduction rule, stable under substitution.* The single
  introduction above tests the witness for being the literal `0`, and a
  substitution can turn a witness into `0`. If instead the fresh variable is
  used exactly when the matrix is literally of the diagonal shape
  `I(y, y; u.h) = I(y, y; v.k)`, the test looks at the matrix alone, and
  substitution for the free variables neither creates nor destroys the shape.
  That calculus, `GPrf`, has seven rules, is closed under substitution by a
  direct induction (`GPrf.subst`), and derives the same sequents
  (`gprf_iff_nprf`). Progress for an arbitrary equation `s(y) = t(y)` is
  recovered through its diagonal lift `I(y, y; u.s) = I(y, y; u.t)` and the
  unconditional equation `sel(y, s(0), I(y, y; u.s(y))) = s(y)`. This is the
  calculus of [`diagonal_guard`](Artifacts/diagonal_guard/).
- *No template.* Transport can be replaced by a rule that is given no
  template at all: from `s = t` and `u = v` infer `v = R(u)`, where `R`
  replaces every occurrence of `s` in `u` by `t`, root first and in one pass
  (`TPrf`, `tprf_iff_nprf`). The rule cannot choose which occurrences to
  replace; transport in a chosen template `h` is recovered with the marker
  `M = I(0, s; u.K)`, whose step term `K` is a numeral larger than `h`, so
  that `h(M)` contains `M` at the template positions and nowhere else. This
  is the rule of [`template_free`](Artifacts/template_free/).
- *Substitution for a parameter.* Transport can also be replaced by the rule
  Param of [`parameter_substitution`](Artifacts/parameter_substitution/): from
  `s = t` and `u = r` infer `r = ψ(s, t, u)`, where `ψ` is `u[t/s]` if `s` is
  a variable, `t` if `u` is `s`, and `u` otherwise. A proper subterm is
  replaced only when the source is a variable (`PPrf`, `pprf_iff_nprf`).
  Transport in a template `h` is recovered under a fresh alias `b = s`, where
  Param at the variable `b` turns `h(b) = h(b)` into `h(b) = h(s)` and into
  `h(b) = h(t)`; the alias is discharged through
  `D_{x,y} (sel(y, s, x) = s)`, proved by cases with the witness `s` and
  eliminated at `y = 1` (`PPrf.aliasE`). The proof of completeness uses the
  variable case and joining at the root only, never the reversal. A
  substitution can turn a variable source into a compound one, so `PPrf` is
  closed under injective renaming (`PPrf.ren`) and not under substitution by a
  direct induction.
- *Substitution at the discharge of a witness.* Transport and DE can be one
  rule: from `D_{x,y} B`, and from `s = t` and `F(s)` in the context opened at
  a fresh `b`, infer `F(t)`, provided it does not mention `b`. With it in
  place of both, the kernel has seven rules (`SDPrf`, `sdprf_iff_nprf`). The
  closed theorem `D_{x,y} (I(0, 0; u.u) = 0)` is proved by cases from a
  computation; a discharge of it that does not use its opened context is
  transport in an arbitrary formula (`SDPrf.tr`), reflexivity is the
  transport of `I(0, a; u.u) = a` along itself, and a constant template gives
  DE (`SDPrf.dE`). Every rule is stable under substitution. This is the
  discharge rule of
  [`substitutive_discharge`](Artifacts/substitutive_discharge/) on the raw
  kernel.
- *QE at a variable or at 1.* The term argument of QE can be restricted to a
  variable and to the numeral `1`: `VQPrf true` has the two rules `qEVar`
  and `qEOne` in place of QE, and derives the same sequents
  (`vqprf_iff_nprf`). An arbitrary target `t` is named by a fresh alias
  `b = t`, whose discharge uses QE at `1` once; QE is applied at the variable
  `b`, and `B(b)` is moved to `B(t)` by the Leibniz rule for `B`. The Leibniz
  rule for a compound formula needs QE at `S z` for its matrix, so the two are
  proved together by induction on the formula (`VQPrf.qELeib`,
  `VQPrf.leibniz`), the Leibniz rule being stated for derivability of the two
  instances over one context, so that no substitution into a derivation is
  used. This is the counterpart, for the kernel, of the clause use without a
  term argument of
  [`deterministic_specialization`](Artifacts/deterministic_specialization/).
  The numeral cannot be dropped: `VQPrf false`, with QE at variables only,
  does not derive `0 = 1` from `Q_y (sel(y, 0, 1) = 0)`, which the kernel
  derives (`vqprf_var_incomplete`). The countermodel reads every variable as
  `0` and every `Q` and `D` formula as true.
- *The shape of the witness of DI.* `DWPrf z v` is the kernel with the
  witness of DI restricted to the literal `0` (if `z`) and to variables (if
  `v`). Each shape alone is incomplete. With `0` alone the calculus is sound
  for the standard reading in which `D_{x,y} B` is read at `x = 0`, and does
  not derive `D_{x,y} (sel(y, 1, x) = 1)` (`dwprf_zero_incomplete`). With
  variables alone it derives no `D` formula at all in the empty context
  without free variables, by a syntactic invariant: there every derivable
  formula is an equation or a closure over an equation
  (`DWPrf.simple`, `dwprf_var_incomplete`). The introduction at a variable
  is enough once every term has a name. `DNPrf` is the kernel with DI at a
  variable only and the axiom scheme `D_{x,y} (sel(y, a, x) = a)` for every
  term `a`, and `dnprf_iff_nprf : DNPrf Γ A ↔ NPrf Γ A`
  (`NativeNamedWitness`). The scheme is the naming matrix of
  [`deterministic_introduction`](Artifacts/deterministic_introduction/):
  opened at a fresh `b` and used at `y = 1` it gives `b = a`, so DI at a term
  `t` is DI at a name of `t` followed by the Leibniz rule. That calculus is
  closed under renaming and not under substitution; its Leibniz rule is
  proved over one context, and a dummy witness in a scope without variables
  is a name of `0`. The two shapes together are enough without the scheme:
  `dwprf_iff_nprf : DWPrf true true Γ A ↔ NPrf Γ A` (`NativeWitnessComplete`).
  The names are derived. With `P` the predecessor term, the name of `P(y)`
  holds at `0` with the witness `0`, and at `S z` with the witness `z`, since
  `z = P(S z)`; so it holds for all `y` by cases with a dummy witness, in
  particular at `S a`, and opening that name gives a variable equal to
  `P(S a) = a`. The two equations of `P` come from a calculus with no
  witness at all, below.
- *The predecessor needs equations only.* `EqPrf` derives an equation from
  equations by five rules: hypothesis, the two computations, transport in one
  term template, and induction for a literal equation with parameters. It
  has no formula other than equations, no coverage `x = 0 ∨ ∃y x = S y`, no
  separation and no case rule. `EqPrf.pred_succ : EqPrf Γ (pred (S t)) t`,
  `EqPrf.pred_zero` and `EqPrf.succ_inj` (`EqKernel`, `EqArith`, `EqParity`,
  `EqCompare`, `EqPred`). The lemmas are those of the `T_eq` development on
  the quotient `EQ Γ` of terms by `EqPrf Γ`; its three Boolean case splits
  and two splits on a selector count become equation cases on a fresh
  variable, that is, the induction rule with an unused hypothesis
  (`EQ.zf_add_zf`, `EQ.mod3_step`, `EQ.sel_cyc_zf`, `EQ.sel_add`,
  `EQ.sel_self_zero`). `EqPrf` embeds in the kernel under any restriction of
  the witness (`EqPrf.toDW`): its induction is QI by progress followed by
  QE. This is the audit of the predecessor in
  [`uniform_raw`](Artifacts/uniform_raw/),
  [`newest_parameter`](Artifacts/newest_parameter/),
  [`parameter_witness`](Artifacts/parameter_witness/) and
  [`no_witness`](Artifacts/no_witness/).
- *A one-iterator selector.* The mode of the single introduction can be read
  off a smaller shape than the diagonal one: progress exactly when the matrix
  is literally `a(x, y) = I(y, a(x, y); u.h)`. That calculus is `MiPrf`
  (seven rules, `miprf_iff_nprf`), and with reflexivity and Eval it is the
  six-rule `M6Prf` (`m6prf_iff_nprf`) of
  [`mirror_core`](Artifacts/mirror_core/). The shape is preserved by
  substitution but can be created by it, so `MiPrf` is closed under injective
  renaming (`MiPrf.ren`), which suffices for weakening under a binder and for
  cut, and not under substitution by a direct induction.
- *Six rules.* Reflexivity and one rule Eval can replace both computation
  equations and transport. Eval infers `r = Φ(s, t, b)` from `s = t` and
  `b = r`, where `Φ` is `t` if `b` is `I(0, s; u.h)`, and `h[t/u]` if `b` is
  `I(S c, a; u.h)` and `s` is `I(c, a; u.h)`. A third case, `Φ = t` if `b` is
  `s`, is derivable from the first through the frame `I(0, s; u.u)`
  ([`equality_from_iteration`](Artifacts/equality_from_iteration/)). With QE, DE
  and the single introduction this is a calculus of six rules, `EPrf`, on the
  unchanged terms and formulas with ordinary substitution, and it derives the
  same sequents (`eprf_iff_nprf`). The computation equations are Eval on two
  reflexivities; transport in a template `h` is one iteration of `h`. This is
  the calculus of
  [`computational_equality`](Artifacts/computational_equality/).
- *Six rules on zero-normal terms.* With the zero computation in the syntax,
  one introduction suffices there too: it is progressive exactly when the
  normalized zero instance of the matrix is literally `r = r`. Hypothesis,
  successor computation, transport in one term, QE, DE and this introduction
  are six rules, `NRPrf` (`nrprf_iff_nprf`, `NRPrf.normal`). This is the
  calculus of [`reflexive_base`](Artifacts/reflexive_base/). Its completeness
  is by translation of the diagonal calculus, with the invariant that a
  literally reflexive hypothesis may be dropped.
- *One successor step.* On zero-normal terms the zero case of Eval is absorbed
  by the syntax, and reflexivity with the single rule Step, from
  `I(c, a; u.h) = t` and `I(S c, a; u.h) = r` infer `r = h[t/u]`, replaces
  both successor computation and transport (`NSPrf`, `nsprf_iff_nprf`,
  `NSPrf.normal`). Equality comes from a pivot of two Steps through
  `I(S 0, x; v.v)`. This is the interface of
  [`uniform_step`](Artifacts/uniform_step/).
- *Seed evaluation.* On zero-normal terms the rule Step can in turn be replaced
  by SeedEval, from `a = b` and `I(S c, a; u.h) = r` infer
  `r = h[I(c, b; u.h)/u]`, whose equation premise is about the seed alone
  (`NVPrf`, `nvprf_iff_nprf`). At the counter `0` the two rules are the same
  inference, which is where the equality reasoning takes place. This is the
  rule of [`seed_evaluation`](Artifacts/seed_evaluation/).
- *One evaluation rule and one introduction on zero-normal terms.* The
  companion calculus of
  [`equality_from_iteration`](Artifacts/equality_from_iteration/) has six
  rules: hypothesis, reflexivity, QE, DE, the single introduction with the
  literal test, and UE, from `I(c, a; u.h) = t` and `I(S c, a; u.h) = r` infer
  `r = h[t/u]` (`ZEPrf`, `zeprf_iff_nprf`). The introduction by cases of an
  equation at the witness `0`, which the single introduction does not have,
  is derived with the zero-normal alias `I(S 0, 0; u.0)` of `0`, with no
  weakening and no cut.
- *A public language for two restrictions at once.* The calculus `PGPrf`
  has the root-determined introduction (progress at a literal equation, cases
  at a compound matrix, no test of the witness) and transport at iterator
  sources only. Every rule of it is a derived rule of the kernel, but a
  hypothesis `x = y` between variables is not a transport source and the
  introduction by cases of an equation is missing. The gated translation
  `pub` replaces every equation `s = t` by `Q_w (I(w, 0; u.s) = I(w, 0; u.t))`.
  Its image is public: every atomic matrix has the guarded shape
  `I(y, 0; u.h)` on both sides (`NFm.pub_guarded`). On it the two calculi
  agree: `pgprf_pub_iff : PGPrf (Γ.map pub) (pub A) ↔ NPrf Γ A`. A gate is
  opened at `S 0` to the wrapped equation `wr s = wr t`,
  `wr s = I(S 0, 0; u.s)`, whose two sides are admissible sources, and is
  closed again by progress. This is the common content of the public
  languages of [`guarded_core`](Artifacts/guarded_core/),
  [`guarded_source`](Artifacts/guarded_source/),
  [`guarded_orbit`](Artifacts/guarded_orbit/),
  [`deterministic_auxiliary`](Artifacts/deterministic_auxiliary/) and
  [`protected_core`](Artifacts/protected_core/). The theorem is proved for
  any gating of equations (`Gating`), and the one-sided guard
  `s = I(w, s; u.t)` of [`mirror_guard`](Artifacts/mirror_guard/) is a second
  instance (`Gating.mirror`, `NFm.pub_mirrored`). `Q` can be removed from
  the public language as well: `NFm.pubD` uses the paired binder with an
  unused witness for every closure, its image has no `Q` and only guarded
  atomic matrices (`NFm.pubD_noQ`, `NFm.pubD_guarded`), and
  `pgprf_pubD_iff : PGPrf (Γ.map pubD) (pubD A) ↔ NPrf Γ A`. That is the
  grammar of the packages: paired binders over guarded equations, with `Q`
  only in the contexts of derivations. The translation cannot be
  dropped: `PGPrf` does not derive `x = z` from `x = y` and `y = z` between
  variables (`pgprf_not_trans`), so on arbitrary sequents it is strictly
  weaker than the kernel (`pgprf_strictly_weaker`). The proof is a reading in
  which a value is a number with a colour, bound variables range over
  ordinary numbers, and an equation holds by number or by adjacent colours;
  every rule of `PGPrf` is sound for it and equality is not transitive.
  The root-determined introduction alone, with unrestricted transport
  (`RDPrf`), is complete on a public language too (`rdprf_pub_iff`) and is
  also strictly weaker on arbitrary formulas: it does not derive
  `D_{x,y} (y = 1)`, which the kernel derives by cases (`rdprf_not_cases`,
  `rdprf_strictly_weaker`). Here the sound reading is the progressive one:
  a closure over a literal equation is read as progressivity. The source
  restriction alone, with the two introductions of the kernel (`TIPrf`),
  contains `PGPrf` (`PGPrf.toTI`), is complete on both public languages
  (`tiprf_pub_iff`, `tiprf_pubD_iff`), and still does not derive
  transitivity between variables (`tiprf_not_trans`): the reading with
  colours is sound for the introduction by cases and for `Q` by progress as
  well. So each restriction is responsible for one loss by itself: iterator
  sources lose transitivity of raw equations, and the root-determined
  introduction loses the introduction by cases of raw equations.
- *Five rules on zero-normal terms, and four schemes.* The clause calculus
  can be put on zero-normal terms with the one successor step as its only
  computation: Refl, Eval, Use, Elim and Intro, each normalizing its
  conclusion, Intro reading its mode off the matrix and the witness (`ZCPrf`,
  `zcprf_iff_nprf`). This is the calculus `C5` of
  [`clausal_single_evaluation`](Artifacts/clausal_single_evaluation/). With
  uniform clauses and the fixed reflexivity clause it has the four schemes
  Use, Step, Open and Close of
  [`clause_contexts`](Artifacts/clause_contexts/) (`ZVPrf`, `zvprf_iff_zcprf`,
  `zvprf_iff_nprf`). Completeness normalizes a derivation of the raw clause
  calculus rule by rule. One case changes under normalization: an
  introduction by cases for an equation whose witness is not the literal `0`
  but has the normal form `0`, which on normal terms would select progress.
  It is made at the witness `w = I(S 0, 0; u.0)` instead, which is
  zero-normal, equal to `0` by one Eval, and not the literal `0`; the
  translation carries the invariant that an assumption `E(t)` of the source
  may be the assumption `E(w)` of the target (`Conv`), and converts at each
  use (`ZCPrf.convEq`). No cut and no renaming of `ZCPrf` derivations is
  needed.
- *Other forms of the source restriction.* For transport in an equation
  template with an uncrossed conclusion, the same restriction needs an
  equation induction and a singleton test, though no logical rule
  (`zprf_iff_nprf`; [`guarded_source`](Artifacts/guarded_source/); class
  `ZKernel`). If transport in arbitrary templates and QE both reverse the
  root equation of their conclusion, it again needs no induction
  (`rprf_iff_nprf`, the module proposed by
  [`reversal_core`](Artifacts/reversal_core/)).

**Which rules cannot be dropped.** Seven of the eight rules of the kernel are
independent of the others (`NativeModels`). A *reading* of the language over
the natural numbers fixes the value of the iterator and the meanings of an
equation, of `Q` and of `D`; one soundness theorem (`FPrf.sound`) asks of a
reading one condition for each rule in use, and each of the following readings
meets the conditions of the other rules and refutes a sequent that the kernel
derives:

The standard reading meets every condition, so the kernel does not derive
`0 = 1` (`native_consistent`). Through the bi-interpretation this is the
consistency of `T_eq` and of iPRA (`teq_consistent`, `pra_consistent`), by a
proof that evaluates iterator terms only.

**Ordinary realization.** `T_eq` is intuitionistic first-order logic with
equality over the same terms, with the two computation equations, coverage
`∀x (x = 0 ∨ ∃y x = S y)`, separation `0 = S 0 → ⊥`, and induction for literal
equations with side assumptions. The reports derive a predecessor, reflection
of equality into a term, quantifier-free induction, pairing and a compiler for
all primitive recursive definitions, in that order, which gives the
bi-interpretation with iPRA.

The Lake library `ConciseIPRA` (root workspace; sources under
[`Lean/ConciseIPRA/`](Lean/ConciseIPRA/), namespace `LeanProofs.ConciseIPRA`)
formalizes three systems and proves them mutually bi-interpretable:

1. **The native scalar core** (`Native`): the calculus of
   [The native scalar core](#the-native-scalar-core), deeply embedded.
   Formulas are `s = t`, `Q_y B` and `D_{x,y} B` only. Derivability
   `NPrf Γ A` has eight rules: Hyp, the two computation equations,
   Tr in one term, QE, DE, DI by cases and QI by progress. There are no
   connectives and no structural rules. The calculus exactly as the reports
   state it, with Tr in arbitrary templates and the witnessed DI by progress,
   is `IPrf` (`NativeInherited`); the two derive the same sequents.
2. **`T_eq`** (`Scalar`): intuitionistic natural deduction with equality
   over the iterator terms, with the axioms listed under *Ordinary
   realization*.
3. **iPRA in the usual way** (`PR`): one function symbol for every primitive
   recursive definition (zero, successor, projections, composition,
   primitive recursion) with its defining equations, `S x = 0 → ⊥`,
   injectivity of successor, and induction for quantifier-free formulas,
   over the same intuitionistic natural deduction.

The main chain (every module except the twenty kernel comparisons,
`ZeroNormalization`, `NativeZeroNormal`, `NativeZeroStep`, `NativeZeroSeed`, `NativeZeroEval`, `NativeInitializer`,
`NativeZeroReflexive`, `NativeZeroClausal`, `FullNormalization`, `NativeFullNormal`,
`NativeInferredWitness`, `NativeVariableSubstitution`, `NativeNewestVariable`, `NativeWitnessDischarge`, `NativeFullSix`,
`NativeFullFive`, `NativeNameClauses`, `NativeOpenClauses`, `NativeExportClauses`,
`NativeVariableClauses`, `NativeProgressive`, `NativeProgressiveRules`,
`NativeProgressiveLeibniz`, `NativeProgressiveEmbedding`, `NativeTargetClosure`,
`NativeProgressiveRoundTrip`, `NativeMixedClosure`, `NativePublic`, `NativePublicD`, `NativePublicNecessary`, `NativeRootDetermined`, `NativeIteratorSource`,
`NativeRawReflexive`, `NativeOneOccurrence`, `NativeNoFixedPoint`,
`ZeroSeedObstruction`,
`NativePrefix`, `NativeUniqueness`, `NativeModels`, `NativeWitnessShape`,
`NativeWitnessComplete`, `EqKernel`, `EqArith`, `EqParity`, `EqCompare`, `EqPred` and
`TeqClosure`) is 4,872
lines; it was 5,984 before the shortening passes. The larger cuts: cut for
natural deduction is a six-line induction on the context, by implication
introduction and elimination, instead of an induction over the seventeen
rules; weakening and substitution share one induction; simultaneous
congruence uses one extra variable; the equality bootstrap of the native
calculus is four single rule applications; reflection of quantifier-free
formulas is proved as an equivalence of Lean propositions,
`mk Γ (chi φ) = 0 ↔ Γ ⊢ φ`, from which the formula of `T_eq` follows. A dependency-closure scan of the
end results, computed inside Lean from the proof terms, finds no further
unused theorem apart from `rfl` lemmas that `simp` uses silently and the
derived rule `NPrf.eqInd`, which only the comparison modules use; a duplicate
of `NFm.map_shift_subst_repl` was removed. In the arithmetic of `T_eq`,
`Q.eqInd` finds its base and its step by `simp` when they are not given, the
computation lemmas of the iterator-defined operations are single terms where
the instance of the computation equation is the statement up to unfolding, and
a quotient induction with one closing step is one line. In the round trip
through iPRA, a recursion which ignores its counter is the iterator of any
provably equal body (`Q.prc_itG`), by one equation induction; that the
iterator respects its body is two instances of it, so no separate uniqueness
or body-congruence induction remains. In the native calculus, ex falso is one
transport of the selector `sel(v, 0 = 0, A)` along `0 = 1` (`NPrf.botE`),
in place of an induction on the formula, and the two collapses of a
trivially guarded `Q` (`NEquiv.qSel`, `NEquiv.qGate`) are instances of one
lemma (`NEquiv.qTriv`). The round trip `T_eq → iPRA → T_eq` of a term is
the soundness of the back translation applied to the evaluation equation of
its code (`RoundTrip.sigma_tau`), not a fourth induction on terms; the
native universal quantifier `all X = X(0) ∧ Q X` is read through the
conjunction lemma and one propositional step; and case distinctions use
`Teq.casesOn` in place of coverage followed by an explicit existential
elimination and weakening. On the iPRA side, uniqueness of primitive
recursion at a parameter substitution (`ToPRA.prec_uniq`, one
quantifier-free induction) gives both the extensionality of the simulated
iterator and the round trip of a recursion symbol, and the successor
equation of that round trip is the translated axiom `FromPRA.ax_precSucc`
rather than a second proof of the same recursion equation. The equality test
of `T_eq` is the symmetric `sel(a ∸ b, b ∸ a, 1)`, whose reflection follows
from the additive witness of the order in four lines, and nine composition
lemmas of native substitution are instances of `NFm.subst_comp`. The
predecessor follows the diagonal lemma of `orbit_equality`: `Q.pred_succ` is
one equation induction on `pred (S x) = x` from the conjugacy of the
saturating counters and `bump 1 0 = 0`, so the comparator diagonal
`cmp (S x) x = 0` and the invariant `sat x (S x) = x` below the cap, each an
induction of its own, are gone (likewise in `EqPred`). The order is
obtained from the maximum identity `x + (y ∸ x) = y + (x ∸ y)` (one equation
induction) in place of a selector-guarded witness invariant, and the
logarithm counter of the pairing from the one-parameter invariant
"`2 ^ i ≤ k` implies `lgc i k = i`", so the monotonicity of `2 ^ x` and
transitivity of the order are not needed. In the native round trip, a
disjunction is read back by closure by cases on a formula (`Teq.caseAll`)
instead of coverage, existential elimination and transport of the selector;
`Q` introduction factors through `D` introduction at the witness `0` and the
dummy-witness elimination `NPrf.dDummyE`, as the article states it; the
forward half of the composite reading of `Q` is derived unshifted and then
shifted; and the elimination of a universal statement at its own variable is
one instance of `NPrf.allShiftE`. The translation into iPRA compiles iPRA
terms rather than iterator terms (`ToPRA.pcode`: projections and
compositions), so the evaluation of a code is a two-case fact about iPRA,
`FromPRA.code (pcode p)` is `sigma p` syntactically, and
`RoundTrip.sigma_tau` is one direct induction; the recursion equations of the
code of `prec f g` are proved once (`FromPRA.code_prec_zero/succ`) and the
translated defining axioms follow from them. In the foundations,
composition of renamings is a corollary of the substitution laws
(`Tm.ren_ren` via `ren_eq_sub`), the congruence and one-variable Leibniz
rules hand `Fin.cases` straight to the Leibniz rule of the calculus,
weakening and the extension maps of `Lindenbaum` are single instances of
`substWeaken`, and the quantifier congruences of `Interpretation` weaken by
`wk` without subset lemmas. In the
round trip through `T_eq`, the steps of each chain of equations are composed
directly instead of being stated twice, and the step shared by three of the
chains is one lemma (`RoundTrip.tau_subst_code`).
