\subsection{Logical changes behind the thirteen-state saving}

Let $p(a,b)=\binom{a+b+1}{2}+b$. PA196 uses

 \I(a,b)=4p(a,b),\quad \M(a,b)=4p(a,b)+1,\quad

\subsection{Uniform proof production under the binary interpretation}

Interpret $\M(a,b)$ as the statement that bit $x_b$ of $x_a$ is one,
$\E(a,b)$ as equality of $x_a,x_b$, implication as implication, and
$\U(a,B)$ as $\forall x_a B$. PA proves that a natural number does
not contain itself as a binary digit position: a nonzero bit at $x$ would
give $2^x\le x$, whereas PA proves $x<2^x$.
Thus the interpreted code 1 has a uniform PA refutation.

For distinct atom labels, apply this construction to the elements of
the given finite set together with the distinguished point. For coincident
labels, membership of a number in itself is false, and a singleton or
the empty set gives the required pointed instance. The guard ensures
that the witness label is distinct from both atom labels. The numerical
code bound ensures that it is also fresh for the property formula.
Equality and membership vacuity then have direct PA proofs.

Annotate every theorem-valued slot in a finite command execution by the
code of its interpreted PA derivation. Axiom supply inserts the uniform
proof templates; modus ponens and generalization transform proof codes;
stack operations transport annotations. A halt exposes code 1 and
therefore yields a PA refutation. All these operations can be implemented
by primitive recursion on finite proof and execution codes.

The required internal theorem is the syntactic statement that this
compiler sends every accepted finite trace to a PA refutation. Its
contrapositive is $\Con(\PA)\to\NH(M_{196})$. Once the uniform
correctness and literal-trace binding obligations are discharged,
together with~\eqref{eq:upstream} it gives the desired mathematical
calibration for the 196-state construction.

\begin{theorem}[Sufficient physical contract]\label{thm:physical}
Suppose a binary table $T$ has the following properties.
Its blank startup reaches a canonical frame representing the source
seed. An invariant $J(i,u)$ holds for that seed and is preserved by
every source instruction. For each nonhalting source instruction and
every valid frame satisfying $J$, the table reaches in a positive number
of steps a canonical frame $F(i',g',v')$, with $g'\ge48$, whose
projection is exactly the source successor. A source halt reaches the
literal halt label, and every finite nonterminal simulation segment has
defined transitions. Then blank-tape halting of $T$ is equivalent to
halting of the source computation.
\end{theorem}

The argument uses only finite trace concatenation, determinism, and
induction. When the invariant and contract witnesses are arithmetized
with PA-provable total constructions, the halting equivalence is
formalizable in PA. It does not by itself supply the logical calibration
of the source theory.

The seed is site 25 with logical register 0 equal to 2 and every other
logical register zero. The independent certificate checker verifies
that its pattern is admitted and that every abstract successor remains
in the appropriate stored set. It checks 274,880 site-pattern pairs and
326,688 successor edges. This closure check is independent of the
worklist algorithm that generated the certificate.

We also feed common mask facts back into the difference bounds and
discard masks incompatible with the resulting bounds, then propagate
again. The final joint certificate stabilizes after three refinement
rounds and contains 274,768 site-pattern pairs. A separate Python
checker verifies its reduction, seed, and every joint transfer directly.
It still yields 4,954 instruction cases. Its additional useful
precondition is that physical register 2 is zero on the positive branch
of physical register 8 at source site 4. Numerical lower and upper
bounds, rather than only zero/nonzero flags, are also passed to the
generalized executor, allowing it to recognize an exact value one that
becomes zero after an extra decrement.

Code $1=\M(0,0)$ is true, while code $9=\M(0,1)$ is false.
Every proposed replacement head and quantifier-commutation head is an
identity. The two membership-rewriting heads follow from equality of
their numerical labels. The existential equality head is true because
its outer relative negation has consequent code 1. The same observation
makes every unguarded gate true, and a failed guard returns true code 0.
The distribution head becomes
$A\to((A\to H)\to H)$, a Boolean tautology, as is the restricted
classical implicational head. Modus ponens preserves truth, and
generalization preserves truth since the quantifier is interpreted as
the identity.

This is an all-instance countervaluation of the numeric rules, not a
claim that it is a first-order model of arithmetic. It refutes a proposed
recovery argument; it does not prove that every possible new PA
interpretation in the modified calculus is impossible. The supplied
script performs 23,328 supplementary finite checks, but the schema
argument above is the proof.

However, the same gate also supplies atomic equality and membership
vacuity at its label $C$. The published completeness proof uses vacuity
at every label distinct from the atom labels, including labels smaller
than them. Restricting the supplied label to $C>H+D$ removes those
instances. Padding a property also changes the bound witness label; it
does not recover arbitrary low-label vacuity. One needs a new derivation
of those instances, or a refutation compiler with a suitable label-order
invariant. Neither is supplied by the padding observation alone.

The ConciseIPRA material optimizes a proof checker for intuitionistic
primitive recursive arithmetic~\cite{ipra}. Its ideas about restricted
equality transport, omitted certificate fields, and shared computation
are useful here. But its target theory and cost metric differ. Equivalence
with iPRA does not provide the needed PA-consistency calibration, and
compressed Python size does not give a two-symbol state count.

The PA196 equality reduction already illustrates the relevant principle:
retain the equality interfaces required by the interpretation, and
derive additional laws from them. Removing quantifier commutation would
need a further idea. The existing reverse membership and basic equality
interfaces do not use it, but vacuity through quantified formulas and
the subsequent bound-variable renaming do. Those are the precise
obligations a deletion must replace.

\section{Reduction searches and why rejected candidates matter}
\label{sec:search}

The experiments preserved the binary alphabet, blank input, working-state
count convention, and full tape endpoint. The record distinguishes three
stages: a proposed rewrite, a finite regression survivor, and an
arbitrary-natural certified construction. None of the new proposals in
this package reaches the last stage with fewer than 196 states.

The reproduced search families include direct context-sensitive state
identification, longer local excursions, head-offset representations,
and two simultaneous folds sharing a newly introduced discriminator.
The last option spends one new state while trying to remove at least two;
counting only the removed states would be erroneous.

A fresh bounded primitive-endpoint screen considered 366,912 one-row
fold mutations. Ten survived targeted examples but failed the full
sampled endpoint suite. A subsequent source-conditioned screen used
69,915 full-frame cases and found no survivor. These are finite rejection
results, not proofs that every possible 195-state table fails.

An additional search considered compressing all incoming excursions of a
candidate deleted state. An odd-length path can sometimes be replaced by
one transition if it leaves every other cell unchanged and ends one cell
from the entry position. For the baseline, the search used local windows
of 16 cells on either side and paths up to 45 steps. It found no state for
which all incoming rows could be eliminated this way. Unknown symbolic
cells were not assigned convenient values to make a candidate pass.

Changing the association of the 201-item axiom word can change both the
number of distinct subtrees and the availability of history-based folds.
The useful cost is therefore the number of physical reader states after
compatible folds, not just the number of distinct internal nodes. The
current cost is $68-6=62$ in that body.

The return scanner imposes an additional constraint. A long zero run
inside a newly arranged path can be mistaken for the delimiter. A grammar
with an attractive node count is rejected if the actual tape execution
returns to the wrong control location. The search tools retain this
constraint and subsequently test the complete instruction contracts.

Source reachability also identifies zero tests whose nonzero arms are
unreachable from the actual scheduler seed. The two concrete inherited
opportunities are the register-6 test at source ordinal 7 and the
register-1 cleanup at ordinal 3773. Removing source occurrences does not
monotonically improve control sharing. A register-6 specialization gives
198 working states and passes all 4,956 arbitrary-natural branch contracts
from supplied source frames. Its blank startup remains uncalibrated:
neither the published clean seed nor a decoded candidate-2 frame was
reached within 1,000,000 literal steps. It is therefore a runtime
experiment, not an accepted blank-tape consistency machine, and its state
count also exceeds the target. A straightforward 202-state cleanup layout
failed its endpoint checks and remains rejected.

There is a concrete obstruction to dropping the first head and recovering
it from its classical dual or from a negative gate. Assign truth to code
zero, interpret implication by Boolean implication, interpret every
universal formula as true, and let both atomic constructors hold exactly
when their numerical labels agree. Then code one is true, but

ponens, and generalization preserve truth, whereas the first head with

Thus the proposed recovery fails in this calculus; invoking explosion
or double-negation elimination to repair it would assume the missing
bootstrap. The archive gives the all-instance argument and an executable
supplementary check.

Its optimization objective is the size of a proof checker in a chosen
software presentation. That metric does not directly measure two-symbol
Turing-machine states. More importantly, replacing the target calculus by
one for iPRA would change the consistency statement. A proposed route
through a stronger intuitionistic theory would require explicit proof
translations relating it to full PA and a concrete compiled state count.
No sub-196 result follows merely from the compactness of an iPRA checker.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Can an axiom-word grammar and its state-sharing decisions be optimized
  jointly, including the return-scanner constraints and context-dependent
  leaf routers? Optimizing them separately can miss a saving.
\item Can a changed association preserve all primitive instruction
  endpoints while exposing a seventh compatible fold in the axiom body?
  This would suffice if no additional states were introduced elsewhere.
\item Can a source-conditioned invariant safely relax one universal
  branch contract and free a useful physical row? Such an invariant must
  cover startup and be inductive through the complete scheduler.
\item Is a preserving duplicate macro worthwhile after accounting for
  the register pairing routine, its scratch registers, and actual reader
  sharing? The clearing push macro cannot substitute for it.
\item Can the syntactic reverse proof compiler of
  Section~\ref{sec:reverse-consistency} be formalized against the exact
  published arithmetic trace predicate, yielding an explicit Lean theorem
  of the PA-provable biconditional?
\item Does a different PA-equivalent calculus give a cheaper axiom supplier
  after compilation, with both directions of proof translation explicit?
  A shorter formula list alone is insufficient evidence.
\end{enumerate}

\section{The machine model and the success condition}
A working state is a state with two defined transitions, one for each binary
tape symbol. The machines use one two-way infinite tape, alphabet $\{0,1\}$,
and left or right unit moves. The initial tape is all zero, the initial head
is at coordinate 0, and the initial state is 0. A separate halt label is not
counted as a working state. Entry into it ends execution after the row's
write and move. A native row \texttt{q b w D r} means: read $b$ in state $q$,
write $w$, move in direction $D$ and enter $r$.

The current machines have 208 working states and 416 defined rows. Their
native halt label is 254; a dense serialization names the working states
$0,\ldots,207$ and halt 208. Large sparse labels do not increase the state
count. The same convention would give 414 rows for a 207-state candidate.
The blank-tape initializer must remain part of the counted machine.

The earlier accepted endpoint was the PA-formalizable equivalence
\[
 \neg\Halt(U_{208},\mathrm{blank})
 \quad\longleftrightarrow\quad \Con(\UU)
 \quad\longleftrightarrow\quad \Con(\PA).
\]
Here that endpoint is \emph{inherited}, not newly derived from a hash, finite
simulation or graph-reachability test. No unconditional nonhalting statement,
proof-assistant certificate or state-minimality theorem is asserted.

The class identifiers are SHA-256 hashes of a deterministic breadth-first
serialization of the rooted graph, with outgoing read-0 before read-1 edges.
Each edge retains its read symbol, write symbol and direction. Start is fixed
at canonical label 0 and halt at $-1$.
\begin{description}[style=nextline,leftmargin=1em]
\item[Class A]
\hash{ab3b7f35756ab763601fae76e24486751d286b699f2ca7d4bedb9b5ea39fe3eb}
\item[Class B]
\hash{baaabd3e109e13e134c05facb1db663bda6a491cf2ea2e7f6ef118beaed0fe99}
\end{description}
The explicit row-by-row comparison, rather than a collision-resistance
assumption about those identifiers, establishes the equivalences.

\begin{theorem}[Literal machine equivalence within each class]
For each pair of current machines in the same class there is a bijection $f$
of their working states and halt label that fixes start and halt and satisfies
\[
 \delta_2(f(q),b)=(w,D,f(r))
 \qquad\text{whenever}\qquad\delta_1(q,b)=(w,D,r).
\]
Consequently, for every same initial complete tape and head coordinate, the
two runs have identical complete tapes and head coordinates at each time,
with states related by $f$. They halt at exactly the same time.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
For either rooted graph, enumerate reachable vertices by breadth-first search,
processing read-0 before read-1 edges. The complete finite tables show that all
208 working vertices and halt are graph reachable. Match equally numbered
vertices in the two traversals. This is a bijection fixing start and halt.
For each of the 416 rows, compare read symbol, written symbol, direction and
the mapped target; all equations hold. The package rechecks 3,744 equations,
one full table per current output against its class representative, including
the representatives' identity equations.

Induct on transition count. At time 0 the tapes and heads agree and states
are related. At a nonhalting time, both heads read the same symbol. The checked
row equation makes both writes and moves equal and relates the successor
states. Halt labels correspond, so neither run can halt without the other.
This is a finite-step induction available in PA; it does not assume any
consistency or claim that halt is reached from the blank tape.
\end{proof}

The dense tables are checked separately: ascending native working-state order
is renamed to $0,\ldots,207$, and 254 to 208. All 416 dense rows match that
renaming for every advertised output. A fresh 48,140-step startup replay
also compares the complete finite-support tape, head and corresponding state
for each class. This is a useful independent finite regression; it is not a
replacement for the all-time conjugacy theorem.

\begin{lemma}[Effective equivalence of the two schemas]
With the same underlying first-order logic and any common additional axioms,
the complete weak and exact filtered-adjunction schemas prove one another.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
An exact witness satisfies each implication required of a weak witness, so
each weak instance follows from the corresponding exact instance. Conversely,
given $\varphi$, instantiate the weak schema with
$\psi(x)=A(x,a,y)\land\varphi(x,\bar p)$. Its upper clause gives
$E(x,b)\to A(x,a,y)\land\varphi(x,\bar p)$. Its lower clause gives
$A(x,a,y)\to((A(x,a,y)\land\varphi(x,\bar p))\to E(x,b))$, which entails the
opposite implication. These two implications give the exact biconditional.
Freshen $b$ first to avoid capture. Each step is a finite syntactic derivation,
so the transformation is effective on instances and finite proofs.
\end{proof}

This lemma is a theory-to-theory equivalence, not a proof of either theory's
PA-equiconsistency. A primary lead is
\href{https://cpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/u.osu.edu/dist/1/1952/files/2014/01/GodelLect060202-n2gdjc.pdf}
{Harvey Friedman, \emph{Issues in the Foundations of Mathematics}, G\"odel
Lecture, 2 June 2002, section C2, page 10}. It states mutual interpretability
with PA for a four-atomic-formula adjunction schema. The displayed bound and
free variables appear inconsistent, and the lecture gives no lower
interpretation proof there. This research does not treat that assertion or a
silently corrected formula as an audited finite-refutation translation.

# A concrete proof-carrying command interpreter

The input interface handles **all numeric command atoms**. It follows the
exact [`decodeAtom`](../../../jamesyc-upstream/pa196/PA196/Commands/Coding.lean):
Cantor-decode the atom to `(tag, fields)`; tag 0 is Shift, tag 1 is MP with the
first decoded field, and larger tags give AX with the stored `y` field before
`x`. Unused field tails need not be zero. `extract_hfs_word` accepts a whole
Foundation HFS-coded atom list. This encoding uses Foundation's **square**
pairing plus one for list cells; it is distinct from the source stack's Cantor
pairing. The file implements both explicitly.
## The intended internal statement

```
PA proves: for every HFS word u,
  wordValue(u, stateCode(0,0,0,0)) = 0
  implies Checker.verifyValue(F(u)) = 2.
```

`2` means an accepted native calculus proof of formula code 1. This statement,
if established, would not yet translate that certificate into a PA refutation
or show that an arbitrary literal-machine halt yields such a command word.
It also does not say that PA proves a halt occurs.

A concrete route to this statement is as follows. Encode the finite tuple
consisting of the live command store, the three certificate components, and a
halted flag/witness. Each update is a fixed composition of Cantor pairing and
unpairing, the numeric head expressions, equality tests, and the imported
`leafCertificate`, `mpCertificate`, and `genCertificate` functions. The
halted case retains its witness. Iterate this total update over the HFS list;
the HFS tail is strictly smaller than its nonzero code, so recursion bounded
by the original word code suffices. The other arithmetic functions involved
are primitive recursive, including bounded square root, pairing and unpairing,
and the numeric expression evaluators. PA proves totality of primitive-recursive
functions. The Python code does not itself establish their PA representations.

The induction invariant is a disjunction. In the live case the command store
is an actual four-field `stateCode` and the two live certificates check, while
`Good(w,pw)` holds for the bounded numeric-stack prefix. In the halted case the
command state is 0 and the retained checker certificate checks formula 1.
The three update cases preserve this invariant using the imported all-model
`verify_head*`, `verify_r8`, `verify_bundle`, `verify_mp`, and `verify_gen`
equations, together with the [stack lemma](../README.md). For AX, all head and
bundle expressions ignore the fourth evaluator argument except `rho8`; the
latter receives the actual `d` in both the command and checker expressions.
For noncanonical atoms the first Cantor tag, not atom equality with 0 or 1,
selects the branch. For Shift, `t+h=1` implies `t=1` or `h=1` in PA. The
zero code for a halted *command state* differs from a live HFS store with four
zero fields, whose encoding is nonzero.

For each of the 38,220 ordered pairs of distinct working states, delete the
first, retain the second, and redirect every target of the deleted state to the
retained one. This includes deleting start state 0: its image is the retained
state. First test retaining both rows unchanged. Then, for each read symbol,

write/direction/target triple (two writes, two directions, and 196 destinations:
all retained states plus halt). The other retained row remains unchanged.

For both source states involved, each scanned symbol, and every allowed local

endpoint matches the single parent step: projected control state, head
position, and every tape cell. During a block all reads must remain within
positions `[-2,2]` relative to its entry head. The child tape is compared on
all five cells, so no write can be hidden inside the window. By induction over
parent steps, a successful complete certificate of these properties gives a
positive-block simulation preserving the entire tape and head at boundaries,
and hence both directions of halting. The local finite checks are executable

PA proof.

The windows are an *overapproximation*, not sampled runs. For each target state,
the script enumerates its incoming transitions and, if necessary, those of the
predecessor state. A first incoming transition constrains the just-written
neighbor. To test a second incoming transition, it reconstructs the predecessor
tape by restoring the symbol read by the first transition, then checks the
second write. A predecessor equal to start state 0 is admitted without a second
history, and all windows at state 0 are admitted. Thus all finite runs from
state 0 on any initial tape are covered, including blank tape; many impossible
windows are deliberately retained.

With `--invariant blank-window`, the script instead computes the least
abstract window reachability set from the all-zero window in state 0.
`--radius R` selects a closure radius of at least two (default 2); a wider
closure is projected back to the five cells used by the local fold test. Each
step overwrites the current bit, shifts the window with the head, and allows
both possible values for the newly exposed bit. The closure therefore contains
every actual blank-start window by induction; it need not be exactly reachable.
At radius 2 the closure contains 2,848 windows, all inside the 3,014
two-predecessor windows. At radius 6 it contains 270,067 windows, whose
five-cell projection has 2,774 windows. It includes an abstract path to halt, so it is not a nonhalting proof.
The same finite local block checks then establish a fold only from blank input.

The control reads the actual sparse-label U209 parent from
`docs/incoming/U208_ConPA_2026-10-29.zip`, member
`U208_ConPA_2026-10-29/baseline/u209.native.tm`, with SHA-256
`d0a155d3c683789f3bf5327c0cfb2a0cfd78076af8f1654d4ca426ccbb604d16`.
It densely relabels all 209 working states and the separate halt, constructs
the radius-2 blank-window invariant, and verifies the reported fold deleting
native 211, retaining 172, and replacing `172/0` with `0 L 217`. The local
simulation passes with block lengths 1, 3, and 7. The more general two-history
invariant includes four spurious windows that prevent this same check, which
illustrates both the value and limitations of context refinement.

The [receipt](two-predecessor-receipt.json) records 196 graph-reachable
working states, no nontrivial exact action-preserving bisimulation class,
3,014 allowed state/windows, no unchanged-row fold, 75,307 retained
fold/read cases after the conservative prefilter, and zero survivors among

## Interpretation

This searches exact one-parent-step simulations, one control identification,
no extra helper state, at most one retained-row replacement, radius-two windows,
16-step blocks, and either stated reachability overapproximation. It may reject
a genuine fold whose correctness needs more historical information, larger
windows, longer blocks, several changed rows, nonaligned source steps, or a
more general representation. It makes no lower-bound claim for 195-state
machines, and a successful table-level fold alone would not establish the
missing arithmetic implication `Con(PA) → ¬Halt(PA196)`.

# Two arbitrary changed rows in a PA196 state fold

This search finds no 195-working-state machine within the following local
simulation template. It is not a general state-count lower bound and supplies
no new PA-consistency equivalence. It strictly extends the previous
[two retained-state rows](../two-row/README.md) and [single arbitrary helper
row](../helper-row/README.md) screens: after deleting one state and redirecting
all incoming references to a retained state, it allows **two distinct rows at
arbitrary retained states** to be replaced. The replacement destinations may
be any retained working state or halt. Other rows retain the original
transitions, except for the target redirection.

The screen considers all 38,220 ordered deleted/retained-state pairs, including
deleting the blank-start state. There are 390 remaining rows, 784 possible
replacement triples per row (two write bits, two directions, and 196 possible
destinations), and therefore 1,781,997,214,233,600 raw two-row assignments
including harmless no-op replacements. The screen also tests zero and one
replacement row. We count working states separately from the distinguished
halt control.

For each parent configuration at the deleted state, keeper, or either modified
helper, and for each admitted five-cell window, the child must match the
parent's **one** transition by a positive block of at most 16 transitions,
reading only those five cells, with the same resulting projected state, head,
and entire five-cell tape. All other parent rows commute in one transition.
The admissible windows are the projection of the inductive radius-six
blank-start closure in the previous search: 270,067 abstract windows project
to 2,774 five-cell state/windows, and the abstraction can reach halt. The
closure is an overapproximation and is not a claim that each window occurs in
the concrete run.

The checks are deterministic. In an unpatched child simulation of any parent
step that fails the template, at least one row modified by a successful
candidate must be visited before that failed run terminates or exits the
window; otherwise the candidate follows the same failed trace. The search
chooses a shortest visited-row set among failed contexts at the deleted and
retained parent states, and enumerates each of its rows as the first patch.
This covers at least one of the two changed rows for every possible repair;
the choice of which patch is first is otherwise immaterial. If the unpatched
child already passes, the search reports that plain witness and does not need
to enumerate additional modifications.

For every first-row triple, the search simulates all contexts at the two
merged states and at the first helper. For each failure, a second patch must
change a row visited on that particular first-patched trace. Intersecting the
visited sets of **all** such failures is therefore a necessary condition for
the second row, even when it is at another helper state. The search excludes
the already-patched row and the deleted state's nonexistent rows, then tries
every retained-or-halt destination and every bit/direction pair at each
remaining row. Finally, it checks all admissible contexts at the deleted
state, keeper, and **both** helpers. No context for a different parent state
needs a multi-step check, because its original transition has not changed
except for target projection. If a first patch alone succeeds, it is reported
as an existence witness and further second patches for that first row need not
be enumerated. Thus the algorithm is an existence screen, not an enumeration
of all possible redundant representations of a successful fold.

For PA196 the unpatched screen has no survivor. The first failure set yields
103,550 first-row locations over all pairs, and the search tries 81,183,200
first-row triples. The failure intersections retain 528,136 second-row
locations, on which it tries 414,058,624 second-row triples. None passes. The
counts and the literal input SHA-256
`e8bbccd4cfa325251ca95066db116b5aa766e404b0971c33c02772be1c3617a8` are
recorded in [receipt.json](receipt.json).

A four-state synthetic control has a genuine two-helper solution: deleting
state 2 and retaining state 0 requires changing both `(0,0)` and `(1,1)`.
The optimized search finds the unique passing pair. A separate unpruned Python
implementation brute-forces zero, one, and all pairs of modified rows and
checks **every** five-cell window at **every** original state; it confirms no
zero- or one-row solution and exactly that two-row solution. This control
exercises the need to preserve first and second patches at different states,
including states other than the deleted/retained pair. It is a finite
cross-check, not formal verification of the entire search.

The restrictions matter: the search does not exclude a fold using blocks
longer than 16, blocks that leave the window, a different representation of
states or tape, multiple parent steps per matching block, more than two changed
rows, or a more precise invariant that excludes some abstract windows.

It covers arbitrary primary register values and arbitrary nonempty finite spare lists, for all 3,809 source instructions and all 4,955 zero/positive branch cases. It covers all 394 candidate rows, counting the separate generic block lemmas. Every contract verifies a positive duration. The checker reports an executable induction over unary blocks, not an independently kernel-checked proof. Its gap-48 control on the unmodified PA196 table covers all 3,812 instructions, 4,959 branch cases, and 392 rows. The resulting reports are `runtime48.json` and `runtime48-baseline.json`; `runtime56.json` is the earlier, weaker candidate check.
